sources.role: the decision that the live animals and high-risk plants party pickers page at eight, and that the one-page clause of inc-087's criteria 7, 8 and 9 is dropped along with req-594, req-595 and the paging and inset half of c-094's outcome. The clause rested on ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-041, which that file heads as the orchestrator's application of Sam's principle rather than a ruling of Sam's: point 3b is about live filtering alone, and the bullet three lines above builds the INS address book list at 8 a page over the same records. The prototype's single page is read off a book too small to need paging, so it is evidence either way only under ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-116, which keeps the prototype to look and feel rather than architecture; ruling:ian-2026-11-11 point 2 is not the ground, being scoped to app/data and data claims. Eight is the INS address book list's figure alone: the transporter list renders no pagination yet, EUDPA-824 being To Do. The 'Selected address' inset comes back with the paging, because req-595's own reason for dropping it was that one page put the chosen row always on screen. req-611 is unaffected: the address book's role-scoped list stays unpaginated, because each frontend reads the whole book to filter by role and pages what is left for display.

claims.statement: The live animals and high-risk plants party pickers show eight of a role's addresses a page.
claims.quote: The pickers page at eight, and the one-page clause of `inc-087`'s criteria 7, 8 and 9 is dropped.
claims.note: New. Answers the report question the bug raised against inc-087 criterion 7.

claims.statement: The one-page clause of inc-087's acceptance criteria 7, 8 and 9 is dropped.
claims.quote: the one-page clause of `inc-087`'s criteria 7, 8 and 9 is dropped
claims.note: New. The clause this ruling withdraws, named by criterion.

claims.statement: Eight a page is the figure the INS address book list already uses, which is why the pickers take it.
claims.quote: Eight is the figure the INS address book list already uses (`insfrontend:src/server/app/features/address-book/list/list.controller.js:49`, `REQ-INS-ADDR-013`).
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: The animals transporter list is not a precedent for how many addresses a page holds, because it renders no pagination today and the ticket to split it into pages of eight is still to do.
claims.quote: The animals transporter list is **not** a precedent: it renders no pagination today, and EUDPA-824, the ticket to split it into pages of eight, is still To Do.
claims.note: New. Refuses a precedent rather than setting one.

claims.statement: Paging the pickers sits on top of the role filtering, which stays as it is.
claims.quote: Paging comes back on top of the role filtering, which is correct and stays.
claims.note: New. Leaves the role filtering inc-087 built untouched.

claims.statement: The one-page clause was a distillation error: it rests on a claim that is the orchestrator's application of Sam's principle on live filtering, not a ruling of Sam's on how many addresses a page holds.
claims.quote: **It was a distillation error, and the error is identifiable.** The clause rests on `ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-041`, which is the orchestrator's application of Sam's principle, not a ruling of Sam's on paging
claims.note: New. Names the claim the withdrawn clause rested on.

claims.statement: Sam's point 3b rules on when results refresh, not on how many addresses a page holds.
claims.quote: It rules on when results refresh, not on how many a page holds.
claims.note: New. The ground on which the earlier claim is read as not covering paging.

claims.statement: The same afternoon ruling builds the INS address book list at eight a page three lines above the sentence that removed the pickers' paging, over the same address-book records, so one page of it holds two incompatible answers, and eight is the one with a requirement behind it.
claims.quote: One ruling, one page of it, two incompatible answers to how many addresses a page holds. Eight is the one with a requirement behind it.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: The prototype showing one page of addresses is a fixture of an address book too small to need paging, not a requirement that a page holds every address.
claims.quote: **The prototype's single page is a fixture, not a requirement.** `prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-063` reads one page off the prototype's own address book, which holds too few records to need paging, so the prototype could not show paging whether it wanted it or not.
claims.note: New. Sets aside the prototype claim behind the one-page clause.

claims.statement: How many rows a page holds over a real dataset that grows is not look and feel, so the prototype is not the authority for it.
claims.quote: It rests instead on `ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-116`, "Prototype is the authority for how things look and feel not how they are architected": how many rows a page holds over a real dataset that grows is not look and feel

claims.statement: The "Selected address: <name>" restatement comes back with the paging, between the search box and the results, in the words both frontends already had.
claims.quote: The inset goes back where it was, between the search box and the results, with the words both frontends already had.
claims.note: New. Reverses req-595's removal of the inset.

claims.statement: The reason req-595 gave for dropping the restatement no longer holds, because the chosen row can be on another page again and a trader on page two would otherwise have nothing on screen telling them what they have chosen.
claims.quote: Once the chosen row can be on another page again, that reason is gone: a trader on page two would otherwise have nothing on screen telling them what they have chosen.

claims.statement: The address book's own role-scoped list stays unpaginated: each frontend reads the whole book because the list endpoint takes no role, filters by role itself, and then pages what is left for display.
claims.quote: The address book's own role-scoped list stays unpaginated: each frontend reads the whole book because the list endpoint takes no role, filters by role itself, and then pages what is left for display. Paging the API would make the role filter wrong.

claims.statement: inc-087 stays done, because it was built as its criteria then read, and the code, the criteria, the requirements behind them, c-094's outcome and the behaviour spec are corrected under EUDPA-827 so a re-distillation does not drop paging or the restatement again.

sources.role: the decision that the exporter clause of inc-087 acceptance criterion 2 is dropped and no EXPORTER role is to be added anywhere. The ruling does not say which override wins when a DR1 judgement and a real constraint the prototype cannot express point different ways on the same difference.
The ruling does not say what a real service does where a real constraint overrides the prototype: whether it keeps today's behaviour or matches the prototype as closely as the constraint allows.
The ruling does not say whether a feature or behaviour a real service has that Design Release 2.1 does not show at all counts as a difference to remove, or is left alone.
The ruling does not say what to do where the code two themes need to touch overlaps, so no boundary keeps their pull requests from conflicting.

claims.statement: In DR2.1 each seeded dashboard notification's document date of issue is worked out from today, as dd/mm/yyyy: a draft's is 5 days plus its position among drafts before today, and every other seeded notification's is 2 days before its submitted date. So the uploaded document in its snapshot always predates submission.
claims.quote: documentDateOfIssue: formatDocumentIssueDate(addDaysToDate(today, -5 - position))
claims.note: The non-draft rule is `documentDateOfIssue: formatDocumentIssueDate(addDaysToDate(submitted, -2))` at line 6557. Only when hasJourneyUpdates (the DR2.1 flag) is set.

claims.statement: Submitting replaces an existing submitted notification with the same reference even when no amendment is in progress, because the match falls back to the notification's own reference; only a reference not yet submitted adds a new entry.
claims.quote: const amendedReference = String(amendingFrom.reference || snapshot.notificationReference || '').trim()
claims.note: Inferred from the findIndex matching on amendedReference, which is the snapshot's reference when amendingFrom is empty.

claims.statement: The demo positions are counted per group: session drafts are numbered from 0 among themselves, session submissions from 0 among themselves, and seeded notifications from the number of session submissions. So a user's fifth draft (position 4) is put under 'Needs inspection' on the changes page while still showing 'Draft', its sixth (position 5) is chosen for inspection, and adding drafts never moves the seeded notifications' positions, while each submission does.
claims.quote: ? enrichDesignRelease2Notification(mapped, index + submitted.length, sessionData)
claims.note: mechanism: numbers dashboard notifications for the position-based demo states. Drafts are enriched with their own map index (8739) and submissions with theirs (8781), so draft, submission and seeded positions can coincide.

claims.statement: In a fresh DR2.1 session the changes page lists GBN-AG-26-7K8M2W under 'Passed inspection', GBN-GP-26-7K8M2T under 'Needs inspection' and GBN-AG-26-7K8M3A under 'Delayed'. The status-change flag is set by position (4, 7, 11) even for drafts and completed notifications, whose own status is kept, so these cards show 'Completed', 'Draft' and 'Completed' rather than the change. With category live-animals only Passed inspection (7K8M2W) and Delayed (7K8M3A) show; with germinal-products only Needs inspection (7K8M2T).
claims.note: Worked out by applying enrichDesignRelease2Notification to the 20 seeded notifications at positions 0-19 with no session drafts or submissions: index 4 is 7K8M2T (draft), 7 is 7K8M2W (completed), 11 is 7K8M3A (completed); preserveStatusVariant skips the status override but hasStatusChange is read from the map regardless.

claims.statement: No trace drives the arrival date radios (Today, Tomorrow, Next 7 days), the date range fields or their date picker, so what they filter and any validation of a bad or reversed date range are not shown.
claims.ref: dashboard.fit.spec.js lines 112-125 (filters asserted present, not used)

claims.statement: No trace shows the 'Arrival date' or 'Newest first' sort applied, or a sort that changes the card order.
No trace shows a search or filter that matches nothing, so the empty state of the filtered results, a tab and a drill-down is not shown.

The drill-downs show 'Show 1-N of N results', implying paging, but no list in the traces is long enough to page, and the category tabs show no paging at all; paging controls and page size are not shown.
The plants dashboard, the inspection 'View requirements' destination, the Messages page and Manage account are placeholders (#), so none of their content is shown.
The traces do not walk /changes?category=live-animals, /actions?category=germinal-products, a category-scoped /inspection, or the germinal products filters.
The traces do not say what makes a notification need action, appear in 'Changes in past 24 hours' or be chosen for inspection; the lists are fixed examples.
The traces do not show whose notifications a dashboard holds (the signed-in user, their organisation or every user), or a dashboard with no notifications yet.
claims.ref: dashboard.fit.spec.js (all tests run on the seeded example data)

sources.role: what exists today and what has already been ruled; the real persistence, validation and cross-service constraints the prototype cannot express

claims.statement: A notification is stored as one document in the MongoDB collection named notification.
claims.quote: @org.springframework.data.mongodb.core.mapping.Document(collection = "notification")

claims.statement: The stored record keeps its structured answers in a notification content sub-object and its obligation fulfilments as a separate list of opaque documents.
claims.quote: A notification's identity and metadata, with its structured content in a {@link Notification} sub-object and its obligation fulfilments as opaque documents.

claims.statement: Each record has a database id.
claims.quote:
@Id
    private String id;

claims.statement: A notification's reference number is unique across all records, and a record may have none (the unique index is sparse).
claims.quote:
@Indexed(unique = true, sparse = true)
    private String referenceNumber;

claims.statement: Each record holds the id of the organisation it belongs to.
claims.quote: private String organisationId;

claims.statement: Each record carries a concurrencyToken version number used for optimistic locking: a save at a stale token is refused.
claims.quote:
@Version
    private Long concurrencyToken;

claims.statement: Each record has a status.
claims.quote: private NotificationStatus status;

claims.statement: A notification's status is one of four values: DRAFT, SUBMITTED, AMEND or DELETED.
claims.quote: DRAFT, SUBMITTED, AMEND, DELETED

claims.statement: Each record has server-stamped created and updated moments, stored as instants.
claims.quote:
private Instant created;

    private Instant updated;

claims.statement: A client cannot set created or updated: the inbound notification shape has no such fields, and the server would discard them.
claims.quote: the aggregate's server-stamped {@code created}/{@code updated} instants are deliberately absent here; a client cannot set them and the server would discard them.

claims.statement: Each record has a submittedAt moment holding the latest submission: set when a draft is submitted, refreshed when an amendment is resubmitted, unchanged when an amendment starts or is cancelled.
claims.quote: `submittedAt` is the latest submission: set when a DRAFT is submitted and refreshed when an AMEND is resubmitted. Starting an amendment leaves it unchanged, and cancelling one returns to SUBMITTED and keeps it.

claims.statement: Each record may carry an expireAt moment, which is never returned in an API response.
claims.quote:
@JsonIgnore
    private Instant expireAt;

claims.statement: expireAt is set at creation only when a time to live in days is configured and the environment is not prod, and it counts from created, so later edits do not extend it.
claims.quote: `expireAt` is set at creation only when `NOTIFICATION_TTL_DAYS` is configured and `ENVIRONMENT` is not `prod`.
claims.note: The expiry mechanics (TTL indexes, removal) are part 2's; this claim records only what the field means on the record.

claims.statement: The record keeps a pre-amend snapshot of the notification content and of the fulfilments, neither of which is ever returned in an API response.
Each record has an answersDifferFromSubmitted flag that is always true or false, stored on write, false on a new notification, and read as false on a record stored without it.
claims.quote: `answersDifferFromSubmitted` is always yes or no, and is stored on write rather than computed on read

claims.statement: Only the notification content sub-object counts when deciding whether answers differ from those submitted: uploaded documents and the fulfilments payload never count as a change, and putting an answer back reads as unchanged.
claims.quote: Only the `notification` content sub-object is compared with its snapshot, both through the same deep clone, so uploaded documents and the opaque fulfilments payload never count as a change. Putting an answer back reads as unchanged.

claims.statement: The fulfilments payload is stored exactly as it arrives and never interpreted by the backend.
claims.quote: `fulfilments` is an opaque payload, stored as it arrives and never interpreted here.

claims.statement: Records are indexed for listing one organisation's notifications by status, newest created first.
claims.quote:
name = "organisationId_status_created",
        def = "{'organisationId': 1, 'status': 1, 'created': -1}"

claims.statement: Records are indexed for listing one organisation's notifications by status, latest arrival date first.
claims.quote:
name = "organisationId_status_arrivalDate",
        def = "{'organisationId': 1, 'status': 1, 'notification.transport.arrivalDate': -1}"

claims.quote: private Origin origin;

claims.statement: The origin holds five text values: countryCode, requiresRegionCode, internalReference, regionOfOriginCode and countrySubdivisionCode.
claims.note: requiresRegionCode is a String, not a boolean, so the frontend's yes/no answer is stored as text.

claims.quote:
@Builder.Default
    private List<Commodity> commodities = new ArrayList<>();

claims.statement: A commodity holds a name, a commodityCode and a description, all text.
A commodity holds a whole-number total number of animals and a whole-number total number of packages.

private Integer totalNoOfAnimals;
    private Integer totalNoOfPackages;

A species line holds a whole-number number of animals and a whole-number number of packages.
claims.quote:
private Integer noOfAnimals;
    private Integer noOfPackages;

claims.quote: private List<AnimalIdentifier> animalIdentifiers;

    private String description;

claims.quote:

    private String unweanedAnimals;

claims.statement: The notification content holds five parties: placeOfOrigin, consignor, consignee, importer and destination.
A party holds a name, an email, a phone and an address.
A party on a notification is a literal copy of the address the trader picked, so later edits or deletions in the address book never reach the notification.
claims.quote: Held as a literal copy of the address the trader picked: later edits or deletions in the address book never reach the notification.

claims.statement: An address is a Standard Address Block of addressLine1, addressLine2, townOrCity, county, postcode and countryCode, all text.
An address's countryCode is an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, not a country name.

    private LocalDate arrivalDate;

claims.statement: The service keeps one summary document per notification in a MongoDB collection named notifications.
claims.quote: @Document(collection = "notifications")

claims.statement: The notifications collection lives in the MongoDB database named by MONGO_DATABASE, default trade-imports-ins-backend.
claims.quote: database: ${MONGO_DATABASE:trade-imports-ins-backend}

claims.statement: The document's id is aggregateId, a string, taken from the event body's aggregateId and set only when the document is first inserted.
claims.quote:
@Id
    private String aggregateId; ... .setOnInsert("_id", aggregateId)

claims.statement: aggregateVersion is a whole number (long) taken from the event body's aggregateVersion and set on every applied event.
claims.quote: private long aggregateVersion; ... .set(AGGREGATE_VERSION, incomingVersion)

claims.statement: referenceNumber is a string taken from data.exchangedDocument.identifier in the event, such as GBN-AG-26-001.
claims.quote: String referenceNumber = text(exchangedDocument.path("identifier"));

claims.statement: organisationId is a string taken from the top-level organisationId of the event body, and it is set on every applied event.
claims.quote: String organisationId = text(body.path(ORGANISATION_ID)); ... update.set(ORGANISATION_ID, organisationId);

claims.statement: status is a free string copied as-is from data.exchangedDocument.notificationStatusCode. The read model does not derive, map or validate the status value.
claims.quote: String status = text(exchangedDocument.path("notificationStatusCode"));
claims.note: The type is String, not an enum, so any value the publisher sends is stored.

claims.statement: The status values the slice shows are DRAFT and SUBMITTED, which the tests send as notificationStatusCode and read back from the stored document.
claims.quote: assertThat(doc.get().getStatus()).isEqualTo("DRAFT"); ... .hasValue("SUBMITTED"));

claims.statement: The slice holds no list of the status values the read model accepts or expects: no enum, schema or doc enumerates them, and the event schema is not defined in this repo.
claims.quote: the schema itself is not defined in this repo.
claims.note: Looked in AggregatedNotification, NotificationUpsertService, OutboxEventType, README, AGENTS.md, docs/architecture.md and the workspace page.

claims.statement: The workspace repo page says notifications with status DELETED are excluded from what the read API returns, so DELETED is a status value the model expects to hold.
claims.quote: Notifications with status `DELETED` are excluded.
claims.note: The exclusion itself is in the query API, part 2. Nothing on the ingest side sets DELETED: it would arrive as notificationStatusCode.

claims.statement: originCountry is a string code taken from data.specifiedConsignment.originCountry.code.value, such as GB or ES.
claims.quote: String originCountry = text(originCountryNode.path("code").path("value"));

claims.statement: originCountrySubdivisionCode is the identifier of the origin country's sub-division whose functionTypeCode content is 106, the UNCL3227 'Region of origin' function, such as ES-CN.
claims.quote: private static final String LOCATION_FUNCTION_SUBDIVISION_OF_ORIGIN = "106";

claims.statement: The subdivision is picked by its function code 106, not by its position in the sub-division list, so a country carrying other sub-divisions first still stores the function-106 one.
claims.quote: A country can carry other sub-divisions too, so the code is picked by its function, not its position.

claims.statement: The read model does not store the event's regionOfOriginCode.
claims.quote: INS uses it for the country subdivision the goods came from, and does not store a region of origin code.

claims.statement: An event that carries an origin country but no function-106 subdivision clears any stored originCountrySubdivisionCode.
claims.quote: An event that carries an origin with no subdivision, such as an amendment from the Canary Islands to mainland France, clears it.

claims.statement: An event with no origin country, such as a lifecycle event, leaves the stored originCountrySubdivisionCode alone.
claims.quote: An event with no origin at all, such as a lifecycle event, leaves it alone.

claims.statement: commodity is a string taken from the first trade line of the first consignment item: its first description entry.
claims.quote: String commodity = text(firstTradeLine.path("description").path(0));

claims.statement: When the first trade line has no description, commodity falls back to that trade line's commonName, and the service logs the aggregate id and version when it does.
claims.quote: The dashboard `commodity` field is the first trade line's `description`, or `commonName` when description is absent. A log line records aggregate id and version when the commonName fallback is used.

claims.statement: Only the first trade line is read for commodity, so a notification with several commodity lines shows one commodity in the read model.
claims.quote:
.path("includedConsignmentItem").path(0)
            .path("includedTradeLineItem").path(0);
claims.note: mechanism: reduces the event's trade lines to one commodity string. Inferred from index 0 being the only element read.

claims.statement: arrivalDate is a calendar date taken from the first transport movement's first arrival event's scheduledOccurrenceDateTime, an instant, reduced to its calendar day in UTC.
claims.quote: .atZone(ZoneOffset.UTC).toLocalDate()

claims.statement: The arrival day is taken back in UTC whatever the server's time zone, because the animals backend writes the arrival at the start of the chosen day in UTC and PIMS needs an instant.
claims.quote: The GBN-AG event carries the arrival as an instant, `scheduledOccurrenceDateTime`, because PIMS needs one. The animals backend writes it at the start of the chosen day in UTC, so `NotificationUpsertService` takes the day back in UTC, whatever the JVM's zone.

claims.statement: arrivalDate is stored in Mongo as a YYYY-MM-DD string, not a BSON date, and read back as a calendar date.
claims.quote: `arrivalDate` is a calendar date: a `LocalDate` on the document and in the API, `YYYY-MM-DD` on the wire, and a string in Mongo.

claims.statement: arrivalDate is stored as a string so the stored day does not depend on where the service runs, and because YYYY-MM-DD strings sort in date order the arrivalDate sort and the compound index work on the string.
claims.quote: Without them Spring Data writes a BSON date at midnight in the JVM's zone, and the stored day then depends on where the service runs. `YYYY-MM-DD` strings sort in date order, so the `arrivalDate` sort and the `organisation_status_sort_fields` index work on the string.

claims.statement: lastUpdated is a moment in time taken from data.exchangedDocument.issueDateTime and stored as a BSON date.
claims.quote: `lastUpdated` is a moment: an `Instant`, RFC 3339 with a `Z` on the wire, and a BSON date in Mongo.

claims.statement: When an event has no issueDateTime, lastUpdated is set to the time the service processes the event.
claims.note: mechanism: lastUpdated falls back to processing time.

claims.statement: The document has exactly 10 fields: aggregateId, aggregateVersion, referenceNumber, organisationId, status, originCountry, originCountrySubdivisionCode, commodity, arrivalDate and lastUpdated. It holds no notification category, no journey or set, no port, no consignor or importer, and no commodity code.
claims.note: The absence of other fields is read from the class having only these. The commodity classCode the test events carry (01059900) is not stored.

claims.statement: A field the event does not carry, or carries blank or not as text, is left as it is stored rather than cleared; only aggregateVersion, lastUpdated and organisationId are written on every applied event.
claims.quote:
if (referenceNumber != null) update.set("referenceNumber", referenceNumber);
        if (status != null) update.set("status", status);
claims.note: mechanism: partial update of the stored summary. originCountrySubdivisionCode is the exception, cleared when an origin arrives without one.

claims.statement: Each event is applied in one atomic Mongo upsert whose query matches the document's id and a stored aggregateVersion lower than the incoming one, so concurrent and out-of-order events converge on the highest version with no read-then-write race.
claims.quote: `NotificationUpsertService` writes each event in one Mongo upsert whose query matches only a stored `aggregateVersion` lower than the incoming one. Concurrent events for the same notification and out-of-order redelivery both converge on the highest version, with no read-then-write race.

claims.statement: An event for a notification not yet stored inserts a new document.
claims.quote: mongoTemplate.upsert(query, update, AggregatedNotification.class);

claims.statement: An event whose aggregateVersion is equal to or lower than the stored one changes nothing: the service does not skip it itself but leaves it to the version filter.
claims.quote: upsert_shouldLeaveStaleEventsToTheVersionFilter_ratherThanSkippingThemItself

claims.statement: A stale or duplicate event for an existing document misses the version filter, so the upsert tries to insert a second document with the same id; that failure is unclassified, so the message is treated as non-retryable and deleted.
claims.quote:
Criteria.where("_id").is(aggregateId)
                .and(AGGREGATE_VERSION).lt(incomingVersion));
claims.note: mechanism: Mongo upsert semantics. Inferred from an upsert whose query misses while _id is fixed by setOnInsert; the duplicate-key error is caught by the error handler as unclassified. The tests prove only the outcome (document unchanged, queue drained), and each such message is counted as discarded and logged at error.

claims.statement: An address is stored as a document in the MongoDB collection named addresses, owned by one organisation.
claims.quote:
/** An organisation-owned address-book entry. {@code roles} can be null or empty. */
@Document(collection = "addresses")

claims.statement: The stored address holds these fields: id, name, addressLine1, addressLine2, townOrCity, county, postcode, countryCode, phone, email (all strings), roles (a list of address roles), organisationId (string), status (ACTIVE or DELETED), createdAt, modifiedAt and expireAt (instants), and version (a number).
claims.note: The stored record has no address type field: roles replaced it.

claims.statement: A stored address's roles may be null or empty: the record itself does not require a role, only the request does.
claims.quote: {@code roles} can be null or empty.

claims.statement: The address's createdAt is set by the database auditing when it is first saved, and modifiedAt each time it is saved.
A stored address carries a version number, which inferred from the Spring Data @Version annotation gives optimistic locking: a save against a stale version is refused.
claims.quote:
@Version
  private Long version;
claims.note: mechanism: version counter on the stored address. How a conflict answers over HTTP is part 2's.

claims.statement: Addresses are indexed by organisation, then status, then newest created first (index org_status_created).
Two addresses are the same address when their ids are equal, whatever their other fields hold.
claims.note: mechanism: identity of the stored address.

claims.statement: An address's status is ACTIVE or DELETED; DELETED is a soft-delete tombstone that is left out of lists but can still be read by id.
claims.quote:
Soft-delete tombstone status. {@code DELETED} addresses are excluded from lists but remain
 * readable by id. The enum is never on the wire.

claims.statement: The status value is never sent on the wire; a read shows a deleted boolean instead.
claims.quote: Soft-deleted addresses expose `deleted: true` on read; the internal `status` enum is not on the wire.

claims.statement: The create and replace request body has the fields name, addressLine1, addressLine2, townOrCity, county, postcode, countryCode, phone, email and roles, all camelCase under their Java names.
claims.quote: Create/update request body. Every field is camelCase on the wire, under its Java name.

claims.statement: A request body that echoes server-assigned fields (id, organisationId, deleted, status, createdAt, modifiedAt) is accepted, and those values are dropped rather than saved.
claims.quote:
Server-assigned fields ({@code id}, {@code organisationId}, {@code deleted}, timestamps) are
 * not components, so a body that echoes them is accepted and they are dropped.
claims.note: The test request_deserialisesFromCamelCaseAndMapsOntoAnEntityIgnoringServerFields sends id, organisationId 'OTHER-ORG', status 'DELETED', deleted true and both timestamps and proves each is null on the entity.

claims.statement: roles is required on create and on update: a missing or empty roles list is refused with 'Select what this address can be used for'.
claims.quote: @NotEmpty(message = "Select what this address can be used for")

claims.statement: A missing roles list is read as an empty list, so it fails the required-roles rule rather than erroring.
claims.quote:
{@code roles} is never null: a missing list reads as empty, and repeated roles collapse to
 * their first occurrence.

claims.statement: A role repeated in the request collapses to its first occurrence, keeping the order the caller sent: CONSIGNOR, PLACE_OF_ORIGIN, CONSIGNOR becomes CONSIGNOR, PLACE_OF_ORIGIN.
claims.quote: roles = roles == null ? List.of() : roles.stream().distinct().toList();

claims.statement: Every role in the request must be one of the five role names exactly; an unknown name (such as TRANSPORTER), a lower-case name (such as consignor), a null entry or a blank entry is refused with 'Select valid roles', keyed by roles.
claims.quote: @AddressRoleNames(message = "Select valid roles")

claims.statement: An unknown role name is reported as a field error on roles beside the other field errors, rather than failing the whole body before validation, so every other field error is still shown.
claims.quote: An unknown enum constant would make Jackson throw before validation, which answers as a `bad-request` problem with no `errors` map and hides every other field error. A string component fails Bean Validation, so the `validation-error` problem names `roles` beside the other field errors.
claims.note: mechanism: roles carried as strings in the request and checked by name. The error key is roles, never roles[1].

claims.statement: A request whose only role is unknown gets exactly one violation, on roles: the one-group rule ignores names that are not roles.
claims.quote: It skips role names that are not roles; `@AddressRoleNames` reports those.

claims.statement: There are five address roles: PLACE_OF_ORIGIN, CONSIGNOR, PLACE_OF_DESTINATION, CONSIGNEE and IMPORTER, each a party or a place a notification can choose the address for.
claims.quote: /** A role a notification can choose this address for: a party, or a place. */

claims.statement: The API describes each role: PLACE_OF_ORIGIN 'Where the animals or goods start their journey', CONSIGNOR 'The party sending the consignment', PLACE_OF_DESTINATION 'Where the animals or goods are unloaded in Great Britain', CONSIGNEE 'The party receiving the consignment', IMPORTER 'The party importing the consignment'.
claims.note: The address book holds no display labels for roles; labels are the caller's copy (README Design notes).

claims.statement: Each role belongs to one of two groups: sending (PLACE_OF_ORIGIN, CONSIGNOR) or receiving (CONSIGNEE, IMPORTER, PLACE_OF_DESTINATION).
claims.quote:
| Sending | `PLACE_OF_ORIGIN`, `CONSIGNOR` |
| Receiving | `CONSIGNEE`, `IMPORTER`, `PLACE_OF_DESTINATION` |

claims.statement: The role groups are internal: they are not part of the API, and a caller only sees them as a refusal. A new role cannot be added without a group.

Each `AddressRole` names its one group (`RoleGroup`), so a new
role cannot be added without a group. The grouping is internal: it is not part of the API, and a
caller only sees it as a refusal.

claims.quote: String message() default "An address can only have roles from one group";
claims.note: README: 'The rule belongs to the address book.' The class-level violation is attached to the roles property so it sits beside the field errors.

claims.statement: A soft-deleted address (a tombstone) is still returned by GET with 200 and deleted: true.

claims.statement: The internal status enum is never on the wire: a soft-deleted address shows only as deleted: true.

claims.statement: GET of an unknown address id answers 404 with the not-found problem and no errors map.

claims.statement: GET of an address id that belongs to another organisation answers 404, exactly as an unknown id does, so the address book never confirms another organisation holds that id.
claims.quote: a cross-organisation request and an unknown id are deliberately indistinguishable, so the address book never confirms that another organisation holds a given id.

claims.statement: A 404 is never a deletion signal: only a 200 with deleted: true means the address was deleted.
claims.quote: A **404** means unknown id or an id outside the caller's organisation — it is **not** a deletion signal. ... Only a **200** response with `deleted: true` means the user deleted this address.

claims.statement: Outside prod a 404 can also mean the address has expired and been removed.
claims.quote: Outside prod it can also mean the address has expired (see below).

claims.statement: An address is replaced with PUT /organisation/{orgId}/addresses/{address-id}, taking a full AddressRequest body, and a success answers 200 with the updated address.
claims.quote: operationId: update-address summary: Replace an address's mutable fields ... '200': description: Updated address with bumped modifiedAt

claims.statement: A replace is a full representation replace: every client-supplied field takes the body's value, and an optional field the body leaves out (addressLine2, county) is cleared.
claims.quote: assertThat(address.getAddressLine2()).isNull(); assertThat(address.getCounty()).isNull();

claims.statement: A replace replaces the address's roles with the body's list, in the order sent.
claims.quote: An update replaces the roles.

claims.statement: A replace keeps the address's id, owning organisation, status and createdAt.
claims.quote: Its {@code id}, {@code organisationId}, {@code status} and {@code createdAt} are kept, and {@code modifiedAt} is bumped.

claims.statement: A successful replace moves modifiedAt later and leaves createdAt unchanged.
claims.quote: assertThat(address.getCreatedAt().toEpochMilli()).isEqualTo(createdAt.toEpochMilli()); assertThat(address.getModifiedAt()).isAfter(baselineModifiedAt);

claims.statement: modifiedAt is an audit timestamp only: it is not used as a precondition on a replace.
claims.quote: {@code modifiedAt} is bumped on success (audit only).

claims.quote: An unknown id, an id outside the caller's organisation, or a soft-deleted tombstone all yield a 404 — tombstones are outside the caller's live set and existence is never leaked.

claims.statement: Every error response is RFC 9457 problem details with Content-Type application/problem+json.

claims.statement: The service gets countries from MDM with GET /mdm/geo/countries, sending the subscription key in the Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key header and the system and blocks query parameters.
The countries request to MDM always sends system GBNAG, and passes the caller's blocks value on unchanged (left out when the caller gave none).
The service gets ports of entry from MDM with GET /mdm/trade/bcp/poes, sending the subscription key in the Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key header and system GBNAG as a query parameter.
MDM's ports answer is an object whose result field holds the list of ports, each with id, code, name and traffic.
MDM's countries answer is a JSON array of countries, each with its codes, names, independence, status, system, subdivisions and blocks; a block has a name, an includeCountry flag and tags.

The service reads an MDM trace id from the x-ms-middleware-request-id response header on the countries and ports calls, logging it when present and warning when absent, and the request still succeeds without it.

- Simpler initial setup — new reference data domains can be added without bootstrapping a new service
- Reduced operational overhead while domains are small

claims.statement: How MDM's product search matches a term: a common name or Latin name returns species rows, one per code that lists the species; a commodity code returns one commodity row with its species nested, and a code is a prefix, so 010 returns every code under it; a commodity description returns species rows plus a commodity row.
claims.quote:
- **Commodity code** (`0102`): one commodity row, species nested. A code is a prefix, so `010` returns every code under it.
- **Commodity description** (`ostrich`): mixed. Species rows plus a commodity row, so the nested species of that commodity come back too.
claims.note: MDM behaviour as documented by the workspace page, not code in this repo.

claims.statement: A search term matches the start of a word ('catt' finds cattle), but two-character terms are not consistent in MDM ('ca' misses cattle, goats and dogs); the service needs at least two characters and the frontend asks for three.

- A term matches the start of a word: "catt" finds cattle, and "bos tau" finds Bos taurus.
- Two-character terms are not consistent: "ca" misses cattle, goats (Capra) and dogs (Canis). Reference-data needs at least two characters and the frontend asks for three, so this only affects other callers.

claims.statement: The service reuses its MDM bearer token until the token's expiry time and fetches a new one before the next MDM call once it has expired; a token returned without an expiry is fetched again on every call.
claims.note: mechanism: caches the MDM bearer token in the Feign request interceptor until its expiresOn. README.md:106 says "The token is reused until it expires."

claims.statement: The stub simulates the DEFRA address lookup gateway's address search at GET /simulator/address-lookup/v2.1/addresses.
claims.quote: @GetMapping("/simulator/address-lookup/v2.1/addresses")

claims.statement: The stub simulates AWS STS, Entra and the address lookup gateway for the address lookup in trade-imports-ins-backend.
claims.quote: The stub simulates AWS STS, Entra and the address lookup gateway for the address lookup in `trade-imports-ins-backend`.

claims.statement: The address search takes two optional query parameters, postcode and find.
claims.quote:
@RequestParam(required = false) String postcode,
        @RequestParam(required = false) String find)

claims.statement: The simulator treats postcode and find identically: the same reserved terms give the same answers whichever parameter carries them.
claims.quote: // Deliberately identical for both parameters.
claims.note: The comment says what find really matches (a postcode, a building name or number, a street, a town) is a question only the real gateway can answer, and dev settles the behaviour.

claims.statement: When both postcode and find are given, the simulator searches on postcode and ignores find, because the term is postcode whenever postcode is present.
claims.quote: String term = postcode != null ? postcode : find;

claims.statement: A search with neither postcode nor find answers 400 with a JSON body whose message is "Either postcode or find is required".
claims.quote: { \"statusCode\": 400, \"message\": \"Either postcode or find is required\" }

claims.statement: The bearer token is checked before the search parameters, so a request with a bad token and no search term answers 401, not 400.
The search term SW1A 1AA answers 200 with JSON holding three addresses.
claims.quote: case "SW1A 1AA" -> jsonOk(THREE_ADDRESSES_FIXTURE);

claims.statement: The three-addresses answer has a header whose totalResults is the string "3", and a results array.
claims.quote:
"header": { "totalResults": "3" },
          "results": [

claims.quote: { "addressLine": "BUCKINGHAM PALACE, LONDON, SW1A 1AA", "subBuildingName": "BUCKINGHAM PALACE", "buildingName": null, "buildingNumber": null, "street": null, "town": "LONDON", "postcode": "SW1A 1AA", "country": "ENGLAND", "uprn": "100023336901", "match": "1", "matchDescription": "EXACT", "language": "EN" }

claims.statement: The fixture is shaped like the real dev gateway response of 2026-09-17, not the published v2.1 specification: everything upper case, country free text rather than an ISO code, no county field, match a string and counts as strings.

claims.statement: The search term ZZ1 1ZZ answers 204 No Content with no body.
claims.quote: case "ZZ1 1ZZ" -> ResponseEntity.noContent().build();

claims.statement: The search term QQ1 1QQ answers 400 with a JSON body whose message is "Requested postcode is not valid".
claims.quote: {\"statusCode\":400,\"message\":\"Requested postcode is not valid\"}

claims.statement: Only the reserved term QQ1 1QQ triggers the invalid-postcode 400: the simulator does not check postcode format, so any other malformed postcode answers the no-results fixture.
claims.quote: case "QQ1 1QQ" -> ResponseEntity.status(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST)
claims.note: The switch has no format check; every term not listed falls to the default branch.

claims.statement: The search term XX1 1XX answers 503 with a JSON body whose message is "Service Unavailable".
claims.quote: {\"statusCode\":503,\"message\":\"Service Unavailable\"}
claims.note: The test calls it the reserved throttled postcode.

claims.statement: The search term YY1 1YY answers 200 with an HTML body, not JSON: "<html><body>Bad Gateway</body></html>".
claims.quote: case "YY1 1YY" -> ResponseEntity.ok().contentType(MediaType.TEXT_HTML).body("<html><body>Bad Gateway</body></html>");
claims.note: The test calls it the reserved proxy-error postcode.

claims.statement: The search term TT1 1TT waits 15 seconds and then answers 200 with the three-addresses fixture.
claims.quote: case "TT1 1TT" -> delayedOk();
claims.note: delayedOk calls Thread.sleep(15_000) then jsonOk(THREE_ADDRESSES_FIXTURE). No test covers this term.

claims.statement: The free-text search terms "Buckingham Palace" and "Downing Street" answer 200 with the three-addresses fixture.
claims.quote: case "Buckingham Palace", "Downing Street" -> jsonOk(THREE_ADDRESSES_FIXTURE);

claims.statement: The reserved free-text terms are fixtures for demonstrating find, not a model of what find matches: a result from the simulator says nothing about whether the same search returns results in dev.
claims.quote: These are reserved terms like the postcodes above, NOT a model of what find matches — that is the question the spike exists to answer, and only the real gateway can. A search here returning results says nothing about whether the same search would return results in dev.

claims.statement: Any search term that is not reserved answers 200 with a no-results JSON body: totalResults the string "0" and an empty results array.
claims.quote: { "header": { "totalResults": "0" }, "results": [] }

claims.statement: Reserved terms match exactly and case-sensitively, so a partial term such as "Buckingham", a lower-case "sw1a 1aa" or a postcode without its space answers no results.
claims.quote: return switch (term) {
claims.note: A Java string switch is exact and case-sensitive, and the term is not trimmed or normalised. The "Buckingham" case is proven by addresses_shouldReturnNoResults_forFreeTextThatIsNotReserved.

claims.statement: Every answer the simulator gives that is not 204 or the HTML proxy error is JSON.
claims.quote: return ResponseEntity.ok().contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON).body(body);

claims.statement: The simulator checks the bearer token the way a real resource server would: signature, audience and expiry, before serving any fixture.
claims.quote: Checks the bearer token the way a real resource server would — signature, audience, expiry — before serving the reserved-postcode fixtures

claims.statement: A request with no Authorization header, or one that does not start with "Bearer " (case-insensitive), answers 401.
claims.quote:
if (authorization == null || !authorization.regionMatches(true, 0, "Bearer ", 0, 7)) {
            return unauthorized();

claims.statement: A bearer that is not a parseable signed JWT answers 401.
A bearer whose RSA signature does not verify against the simulator's Entra signing key answers 401.
claims.quote:
if (!jwt.verify(new RSASSAVerifier(keys.entraKey().toRSAPublicKey()))) {
                return unauthorized();
claims.note: So only a token issued by the stub's own Entra simulator is accepted.

claims.statement: A bearer whose audience is missing or does not contain the expected audience answers 401, and the simulator logs a warning naming the audience it rejected.
claims.quote: log.warn("Address lookup simulator rejected a bearer with audience {}", claims.getAudience());

claims.statement: A bearer with no expiry time, or one whose expiry has passed, answers 401.
claims.quote:
if (claims.getExpirationTime() == null || claims.getExpirationTime().before(new Date())) {
            return unauthorized();

claims.statement: Every 401 answers the JSON body { "statusCode": 401, "message": "Unauthorized. Access token is missing or invalid." }, word for word what the real gateway's validate-jwt policy returned in dev on 2026-09-17.
claims.quote: { \"statusCode\": 401, \"message\": \"Unauthorized. Access token is missing or invalid.\" }

claims.statement: A 401 carries no WWW-Authenticate header, matching the real gateway.
claims.quote: The gateway sends no {@code WWW-Authenticate} header with it, and neither does this.

claims.statement: The expected audience is set by address-lookup-simulator.expected-audience, from ADDRESS_LOOKUP_SIMULATOR_EXPECTED_AUDIENCE, defaulting to api://33333333-3333-3333-3333-333333333333.
claims.quote: expected-audience: ${ADDRESS_LOOKUP_SIMULATOR_EXPECTED_AUDIENCE:api://33333333-3333-3333-3333-333333333333}

claims.statement: The expected audience must match the Scope that ins-backend requests once /.default is stripped, api:// prefix included; the dev gateway rejects the bare GUID, so the simulator does too.
claims.quote: `address-lookup-simulator.expected-audience` must match the `Scope` that ins-backend requests once `/.default` is stripped, `api://` prefix included. The gateway in dev rejects the bare GUID, so the simulator does too.

claims.statement: The local profile does not change the address lookup simulator's settings, so a locally run stub expects the same default audience.
claims.quote:
sts-simulator:
  issuer: ${STS_SIMULATOR_ISSUER:http://localhost:8098/}
claims.note: The local profile overrides only the STS issuer among the simulators; it has no address-lookup-simulator block.

claims.statement: The class Javadoc says find and the truncation and find fixtures are a later iteration, though the controller now handles find and two free-text fixtures; no truncation fixture exists.
claims.quote: Only the fixtures iteration 1 needs are wired here; {@code find} and the truncation/find fixtures are iteration 2.
claims.note: The Javadoc is stale against the code below it on find. A truncation fixture (more results than a page holds) is named but not built.

claims.statement: The simulator has no fixture that returns more than three addresses, an address outside England, a Welsh-language address or a paged result; it takes no parameter other than postcode and find.
claims.note: Looked at every case of the switch and both fixtures. The Javadoc names truncation fixtures as not built.

claims.statement: The stub answers GET /mdm/geo/countries, standing in for MDM's countries endpoint through APIM.
claims.quote: @GetMapping(value = "/mdm/geo/countries")

claims.statement: The countries endpoint requires an Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key request header.
claims.quote: @RequestHeader(OCP_APIM_SUBSCRIPTION_KEY) String ocpApimSubscriptionKey

claims.statement: Any value of the subscription-key header is accepted: the stub never checks it.
claims.quote: headers.add(OCP_APIM_SUBSCRIPTION_KEY, "any-value-at-all");
claims.note: The handler never reads ocpApimSubscriptionKey, and the tests send an arbitrary value and get 200.

claims.statement: A call to the countries endpoint without the subscription-key header is refused with 400 Bad Request.
claims.quote: getCountries_shouldRefuseTheCall_whenTheSubscriptionKeyHeaderIsMissing() ... .andExpect(status().isBadRequest());
claims.note: The 400 is Spring's own answer for a missing required header; the README says GlobalExceptionHandler answers only application exceptions.

claims.statement: The countries endpoint accepts an optional system query parameter and ignores it: the answer is the same whatever system is given.
claims.quote: @RequestParam(value = "system", required = false) String system
claims.note: system is bound but never used in the handler body.

claims.statement: The countries endpoint accepts an optional blocks query parameter.
claims.quote: @RequestParam(value = "blocks", required = false) String blocks

claims.statement: When blocks is absent or blank, the countries endpoint answers the whole saved country list.
claims.quote: JsonNode body = blocks == null || blocks.isBlank() ? countries : inBlock(countries, blocks);

claims.statement: When blocks names a block, the countries endpoint answers only the country records that carry a block entry whose name equals it exactly.
claims.quote:
return StreamSupport.stream(country.path("blocks").spliterator(), false)
        .anyMatch((entry) -> block.equals(entry.path("name").asText()));
claims.note: Only the record's top-level blocks array is read; a subdivision's blocs are not consulted. The match is case-sensitive and blocks is a single name, not a list.

claims.statement: A filtered countries answer keeps the saved file's order.
The blocks filter keeps a record carrying the block whatever that block entry's includeCountry says, as MDM does.
claims.quote: `blocks` keeps the records that carry that block whatever `includeCountry` says, as MDM does.

claims.statement: The saved country records hold membership of the GBNAG_SPS_EX block only, so any other block answers an empty list.
claims.quote: The saved records hold the membership of `GBNAG_SPS_EX` only, so any other block answers an empty list.

claims.statement: The countries endpoint answers 200 with a JSON array as its body, both whole and filtered.
claims.quote: return withTraceHeader(ResponseEntity.ok()).body(body);

claims.statement: The countries endpoint serves the country records saved from MDM in responses/countriesResponse.json.
claims.quote: `GET /mdm/geo/countries` answers the country records saved from MDM in `src/main/resources/responses/countriesResponse.json`, whole.

claims.statement: The saved country list is read once, when the stub starts, and every call answers from that copy.
claims.note: Read in the controller's constructor, so a change to the file needs a restart. If the file cannot be read, the controller cannot be built and the stub fails to start.

claims.statement: Every MDM stub answer carries the header x-ms-middleware-request-id with the value stub-trace-id.
claims.quote: return response.header("x-ms-middleware-request-id", "stub-trace-id");
claims.note: Shared helper; the countries endpoint uses it, and the test matcher carriesTheStubTraceHeader asserts it.

claims.statement: The stub loads a saved response by its classpath resource name and parses it as JSON.
claims.quote:
var inputStream = getClass().getClassLoader()
          .getResourceAsStream(fileName);
claims.note: mechanism: reads the saved MDM response files from src/main/resources/responses.

claims.statement: When a saved response file is missing, loading it fails with an error naming the file.
claims.quote: throw new IllegalArgumentException("File not found: " + fileName);
claims.note: mechanism: the not-found error is wrapped in the general read failure below.

claims.statement: When a saved response file is missing or unreadable, the stub logs an error naming the file and throws "Failed to read from json file: <file>".
claims.quote:
log.error("Failed to read from JSON file: {}", fileName, e);
      throw new RuntimeException("Failed to read from json file: " + fileName, e);

claims.quote: "countryUUID": { "content": "013767da-55b6-4a0b-8db4-76b83e779ecb", "schemeId": "MDM-COUNTRY", "schemeAgencyId": "DEFRA" }

claims.statement: Every record's ISONumeric, alpha2 and alpha3 each carry listId "ISO-3166-3", listAgencyId "ISO" and listVersionId "2024-06".
claims.ref: src/main/resources/responses/countriesResponse.json:13-30 (record 1), and the same in all 83 records of the slice
claims.quote: "listId": "ISO-3166-3", "listAgencyId": "ISO", "listVersionId": "2024-06"

claims.statement: ISONumeric is a string with no leading zeros, so a code below 100 is one or two digits: Armenia is "51", Bahrain "48", American Samoa "16", Angola "24" and Bhutan "64".
claims.note: A consumer that matches or shows the three-digit ISO numeric form has to pad these itself.

claims.statement: Every record in the slice has system "gbnag".
claims.ref: src/main/resources/responses/countriesResponse.json:32 (record 1), and the same in all 83 records of the slice
claims.quote: "system": "gbnag"

claims.statement: No record in the slice has a system alias: systemAlias, systemAlpha2 and systemAlpha3 are null in all 83.
claims.ref: src/main/resources/responses/countriesResponse.json:33-35 (record 1), and the same in all 83 records of the slice
claims.quote: "systemAlias": null, "systemAlpha2": null, "systemAlpha3": null

claims.statement: In every record of the slice, effectiveAlpha2 and effectiveAlpha3 are the same as the ISO alpha2 and alpha3 values.
claims.ref: src/main/resources/responses/countriesResponse.json:20, 26, 37-38 (record 1), and the same in all 83 records of the slice
claims.quote: "value": "AW" | "value": "ABW" | "effectiveAlpha2": "AW", "effectiveAlpha3": "ABW"

claims.statement: No record in the slice carries a subdivision: subDivisions is an empty list in all 83.
claims.ref: src/main/resources/responses/countriesResponse.json:39 (record 1), and the same in all 83 records of the slice
claims.quote: "subDivisions": []

claims.statement: independent is false in 80 of the 83 records, and the records for Chad, Oman and Cuba have no independent key at all.
claims.ref: src/main/resources/responses/countriesResponse.json:31 (record 1); Chad at 2492-2530, Oman at 2791-2829, Cuba at 3050-3088
claims.quote: "independent": false

claims.statement: independent does not say whether a country is sovereign: it is false for sovereign states such as Japan, Canada and the United States as well as for territories such as Aruba and Greenland.
claims.quote: "independent": false, "system": "gbnag", "systemAlias": null, "systemAlpha2": null, "systemAlpha3": null, "effectiveAlias": "Japan"
claims.note: Inferred because the same false value sits on every record that has the key, whatever its status, so nothing in the slice can tell a country from a territory.

claims.statement: The list served as countries includes territories, dependencies and Crown Dependencies alongside states, among them Aruba, Reunion, American Samoa, Greenland, Jersey, the Isle of Man, the British Indian Ocean Territory, the Cocos (Keeling) Islands, Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba, Sint Maarten, the Aland Islands, Guadeloupe, Martinique and the United States Minor Outlying Islands.
claims.ref: src/main/resources/responses/countriesResponse.json:36 (Aruba), 686 (Jersey), 3004 (Isle of Man), 646 (British Indian Ocean Territory (the)), 3213 (United States Minor Outlying Islands (the))
claims.quote: "effectiveAlias": "Jersey" | "effectiveAlias": "Isle of Man" | "effectiveAlias": "British Indian Ocean Territory (the)"

claims.statement: effectiveAlias names follow the ISO 3166 short-name style, with the definite article in brackets after the name: "Niger (the)", "Cook Islands (the)", "Turks and Caicos Islands (the)", "United States of America (the)", "Marshall Islands (the)" and "Syrian Arab Republic (the)".
claims.quote: "effectiveAlias": "Niger (the)" | "effectiveAlias": "United States of America (the)" | "effectiveAlias": "Syrian Arab Republic (the)"

claims.statement: Other effectiveAlias names use the ISO long-form qualifiers in brackets or after a comma: "Moldova (the Republic of)", "Bolivia (Plurinational State of)", "Korea (the Democratic People's Republic of)", "Palestine, State of", "Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha", "Virgin Islands (British)" and "Sint Maarten (Dutch part)".
claims.quote: "effectiveAlias": "Moldova (the Republic of)" | "effectiveAlias": "Palestine, State of" | "effectiveAlias": "Virgin Islands (British)"

claims.statement: effectiveAlias names are written without diacritics: "Reunion", "Saint Barthelemy" and "Aland Islands".
claims.quote: "effectiveAlias": "Reunion" | "effectiveAlias": "Saint Barthelemy" | "effectiveAlias": "Aland Islands"

claims.statement: 10 of the 83 records carry block entries, two each: Hungary, Latvia, Cyprus, Greece, Czechia, Denmark, Malta, Switzerland, Slovakia and Poland. The other 73 have an empty blocks list. No block entry in the slice has a tag, and every entry has includeCountry true.
claims.quote: "blocks": [ { "includeCountry": true, "tags": [] }, { "name": "GBNAG_SPS_EX", "includeCountry": true, "tags": [] } ]
claims.note: Switzerland is in the GBNAG_SPS_EX block with the nine EU members of the slice. What the block means is not stated in this file.

claims.statement: The slice does not say what the GBNAG_SPS_EX block stands for or which block the unnamed first entry of each blocked record belongs to.
claims.ref: src/main/resources/responses/countriesResponse.json:440-450 (Hungary's blocks, the first in the slice); looked through every block entry in lines 1 to 3418
claims.note: The block name is a code only, and the unnamed entry has no name key. How the stub filters on the blocks parameter belongs to the countries endpoint part.

claims.statement: The ports of entry call must carry an Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key header.
claims.quote: @RequestHeader(OCP_APIM_SUBSCRIPTION_KEY) String ocpApimSubscriptionKey,

claims.statement: The ports of entry call takes an optional system query parameter.
claims.quote: @RequestParam(value = "system", required = false) String system) {

claims.statement: The system parameter changes nothing: the stub answers the same records whatever system is named, or none.
claims.quote: return withTraceHeader(ResponseEntity.ok()).body(ports);

claims.statement: The ports of entry call answers 200 OK.
claims.quote: return withTraceHeader(ResponseEntity.ok()).body(ports);

claims.quote: return response.header("x-ms-middleware-request-id", "stub-trace-id");

claims.statement: A bearer whose audience list holds several values is accepted when any one of them is the expected audience, because the check asks only whether the list contains it.
claims.quote: if (claims.getAudience() == null || !claims.getAudience().contains(expectedAudience)) {

claims.statement: The simulator checks only the bearer's signature, audience and expiry: it does not check the issuer, subject, issue time or not-before time, so a token signed by the stub's Entra key with the right audience and a future expiry is accepted whatever else it carries.
claims.note: validateBearer reads no claim other than audience and expiration time before returning null (accept).

sources.role: what exists today and what has already been ruled

claims.statement: The live-animals notification set is identified as 'live-animals' and every one of its pages hangs off the base path /live-animals.
claims.quote:
export const SET_ID = 'live-animals'
export const SET_BASE = `/${SET_ID}`

claims.statement: The whole service's routes are this one set's: the router exports the live-animals plugin as its only service routes, so live animals is the only notification set the frontend serves today.
claims.quote: export { liveAnimals as serviceRoutes } from './routes-live-animals.js'

claims.statement: Every page of the set renders inside one shared layout, shared/layout.njk.
claims.quote: export const LAYOUT = 'shared/layout.njk'

claims.statement: The set's templates are resolved under live-animals/journeys/linear.
claims.quote: export const TEMPLATES = 'live-animals/journeys/linear'

claims.statement: The set keeps five separate session cookies: the journeys the browser knows, the flow-only answers, address handshake tokens, the added-address banner, and reviewed-concurrency tokens.
claims.quote:
export const SESSION_COOKIE_NAMES = {
  knownJourneys: 'liveAnimalsKnownJourneys',
  flowOnlyAnswers: 'liveAnimalsFlowOnlyAnswers',
  addressHandshakeTokens: 'liveAnimalsAddressHandshakeTokens',
  addedAddressBanner: 'liveAnimalsAddedAddressBanner',
  reviewedConcurrencyTokens: 'liveAnimalsReviewedConcurrencyTokens'
}

claims.statement: Every request into the set enters the set's context before authentication runs, and every route is wrapped so it runs in that context.
claims.note: mechanism: carries the ambient set id through a request so set-keyed stores (dispatch index, journey flow, obligations, records, session) resolve to this set.

claims.statement: The entry guard runs before every handler in the set and, when it names a target, redirects there and stops the request.
Boot refuses the set when two pages both claim to collect the same obligation, naming the obligation and both pages.
Boot refuses the set when any obligation that is not system-populated is collected by no page, naming each uncovered obligation.
An obligation id may not contain a path metacharacter ('.', '[' or ']'), and boot refuses one that does.
claims.quote:
const ID_UNSAFE = /[.[\]]/
...
      throw new Error(
        `Obligation id "${obligation.name}" (at ${templatePath}) contains a path ` +
          `metacharacter ('.', '[' or ']') — ids must be path-safe`
      )

claims.statement: Boot also refuses the set when a feature's fulfilment bindings do not cover every obligation, and when a party binding is not scalar.
claims.quote:
assertObligationPurity()
        assertFulfilmentBindingCoverage()
        assertPartyBindingsAreScalar()
claims.note: The assertion names say what they refuse; the assertion bodies live in bridge/fulfilment-registry.js and features/addresses/assert-party-bindings.js, outside this part's slice.

claims.statement: A derived page or section gate consulted before the obligation-to-page index is built raises an error rather than silently gating every page and section out.
claims.quote:
throw new Error(
    'Derived gate consulted before the dispatch index exists — call ' +
      'buildDispatch() at boot first (an empty index would silently gate ' +
      'every page and section out)'
  )

claims.statement: Reading the obligation-to-page index before boot answers as if it were empty rather than raising, so the gate layer can tell the un-booted case apart itself.
claims.note: mechanism: the set-keyed dispatch store, which holds the obligation owner, collects, slug and validation maps per page.

claims.statement: The journey flow is unconfigured until boot calls configureJourneyFlow, and asking it for a row status, the INS type-question URL or an entry-guard target before then raises 'journey flow not configured'.

The set configures its journey flow from eight things: the sections, the task rows, the row-status rule, the INS type-question URL, the flow-only keys, the entry-guard target, the layout and the section-caption lookup.
claims.quote:
configureJourneyFlow(SET_ID, {
          sections,
          taskRows,
          rowStatus,
          insTypeQuestionUrl,
          flowOnlyKeys: FLOW_ONLY_KEYS,
          entryGuardTarget,
          layout: LAYOUT,
          sectionCaption: sectionCaptionOf
        })

claims.statement: Ten route bundles serve pages the journey flow does not sequence at all: the overview (hub), the party picker, the address return, the party edit, transporter add, commercial transporter details, private transporter details, cancel amend, notification actions and delete notification.
claims.quote:
...partyPicker.routes,
  ...addressReturn.routes,
  ...partyEdit.routes,
...
  ...transporterAdd.routes,
  ...commercialTransporterDetails.routes,
  ...privateTransporterDetails.routes,
...
  ...cancelAmend.routes,
  ...notificationActions.routes,
  ...deleteNotification.routes,
claims.note: These bundles are reachable by URL but are in no journey section, so Save and continue never lands on them and the task list never counts them.

claims.statement: A page claims an obligation by naming it in the `collects` list on the page's meta, and the page that claims a group also owns every obligation nested inside it, because ownership is resolved by walking up the obligation's dotted path to the nearest claimed ancestor.
A page that states validation rules can have them run against already-stored answers by a caller holding only its page id, which is how the task list and the review page re-check saved answers.
The start section holds one page, the dashboard.
The about-the-consignment section holds three pages in order: origin, commodities and import reason.
The description-of-the-goods section holds three pages in order: consignment details, animal identification and additional details.
The transport-and-arrival section holds three pages in order: port of entry, transit countries and transporters.
The documents section holds one page, accompanying documents.
The consignment-parties section holds three pages in order: CPH number, permanent address and addresses.
claims.note: CPH number and permanent address come before the addresses page in the flow, although the addresses task row leads with the addresses page.

claims.statement: The review section holds three pages in order, the notification view, the declaration and the confirmation, and opens only when the journey is ready for check your answers.
The review section is the only section with an authored gate; every other section's availability is derived from its obligations.
claims.quote: gate: (scope) => scope.readyForCheckYourAnswers,
claims.note: No other section entry in the sections array carries a `gate` key.

claims.statement: A journey is ready for check your answers when every task row leaves the trader nothing to do, that is when each row reads fulfilled, not applicable or optional.
claims.quote:
/** True for a status that leaves nothing for the trader to do: fulfilled, not
 * applicable or optional. */
export const rowReady = (status) =>
  status === FULFILLED || status === NA || status === OPTIONAL

export const readyForCheckYourAnswers = (answers, inScope, evaluation) =>
  journeyTaskRows().every((row) =>
    rowReady(journeyRowStatus(row, answers, inScope, evaluation))
  )

claims.statement: A page with no authored gate applies when at least one obligation it collects is in scope; a page that collects nothing always applies.
An authored gate on a page replaces both the derived scope test and the required-earlier-answer test, so a page that states its own gate is never held back for a missing earlier answer.
claims.quote:
const prerequisitesAllowPage = (page, scope) =>
  Boolean(page.gate) || earliestMissingAnswerPage(page.id, scope) === undefined

export const pageGatePasses = (page, scope) =>
  prerequisitesAllowPage(page, scope) && pageAppliesTo(page, scope)

claims.statement: A section's prerequisite answers are those of its first page, so a section is held back by the same earlier answers its first page needs.
A page is held back only by those enforced answers whose own page comes earlier than it in the journey's page order, so an enforced answer asked later in the flow never blocks an earlier page.
claims.quote:
const continueOwnersBefore = (flowIndex) =>
  continueObligationOwners().filter(
    (owner) => owner.flowIndex !== -1 && owner.flowIndex < flowIndex
  )

const continuePrereqsBefore = (flowIndex) =>
  continueOwnersBefore(flowIndex).map((owner) => owner.id)

claims.statement: When a trader reaches a page whose required earlier answers are missing, they are sent to the page that asks for the earliest missing one in page order, and the page they tried to open is recorded with every missing answer id.
Save and continue goes to the next page in journey order that applies to this consignment, skipping any page that does not apply.
claims.quote:
const next = pages
    .slice(index + 1)
    .filter(isStep)
    .find((page) => pageAppliesTo(page, scope))
  if (!next) {
    return undefined
  }

claims.statement: Only a page that is not a sub-page and belongs to a task row counts as a step Save and continue can land on.
The permanent address page is in the journey's sections but in no task row, so it is reachable only from another page, not from the task list.
claims.quote: pages: [cphNumberPage, permanentAddressPage, addressesPage]
claims.note: The 11 task rows list the CPH number page (inside the addresses row) but never the permanent address page.

claims.statement: Past the last step of the journey, Save and continue has no next page to offer.
Pressing Save and continue on a page that is in no journey section raises an error naming the page.
A task row's link opens the first of its pages whose gate passes, and falls back to the row's first page when none does.
The task rows shown under a section are those whose first page sits in that section, ordered by where that page falls in the section.
claims.quote:
const firstPageIndexIn = (section, row) =>
  section.pages.findIndex((page) => page.id === row.pages[0].id)

export const taskRowsOfSection = (section) =>
  journeyTaskRows()
    .filter((row) => firstPageIndexIn(section, row) !== -1)
    .sort(
      (rowA, rowB) =>
        firstPageIndexIn(section, rowA) - firstPageIndexIn(section, rowB)
    )

The import reason task row covers the import reason page alone.

The animal identification task row covers the animal identification page, counts only the animal identifiers of each commodity line, is shown as a conditional row, and reads not applicable until the consignment has at least one commodity line.

claims.statement: The addresses task row groups two pages, the addresses page and the CPH number page, and does not read as finished until every animal that needs a permanent address has one, even when all the answers the two pages collect are given.

A row's status is worked out in three steps: a row whose condition does not apply reads not applicable; otherwise the row's parts are rolled up into a status; and a rolled-up fulfilled is demoted to in progress when the row's extra answer is still missing.
A row that does not author its own parts counts the obligations its pages collect, so the task list follows the dispatch ownership map by default.
claims.quote:
export const rowParts = (row) =>
  row.parts ?? row.pages.flatMap((page) => collectsOf(page.id))

claims.statement: A section's status rolls up every obligation its pages collect, in page order.
claims.quote:
export const sectionObligationIds = (section) =>
  section.pages.flatMap((page) => collectsOf(page.id))

export const sectionStatus = (section, answers, inScope, evaluation) =>
  statusOf(sectionObligationIds(section), answers, inScope, evaluation)

claims.statement: A task row whose already-saved answers no longer pass its own pages' rules is demoted back to 'To do' on the overview, however complete the engine counts it.
A row's stored-answer errors are its pages' stored-answer errors merged, and a page that states no rules of its own contributes none.
claims.note: mechanism: merges each page's stored-answer error map for one task row.

claims.statement: A card on the review page shows one broken-answer message, the first its rows produce, not every one behind it.

The entry guard applies to any page path under /live-animals/notifications/<journeyId>/ and leaves the create path, the four notification action paths and the origin page (with anything under it) alone.
A trader who opens a guarded page of a notification with no answer entered yet is sent to that notification's origin page.
That redirect is logged once at info with the notification's id and the path the trader asked for, under the message 'No answer entered, sent to the first page'.
claims.quote:
request.logger.info(
    { journeyId: journey.journeyId, path: request.path },
    'No answer entered, sent to the first page'
  )

claims.statement: A notification counts as having committed answers when any stored key is a trader-entered obligation (not a system-populated one) and holds an answer; a flow-only key such as the declaration does not count.
claims.note: A flow-only key is not in the obligation manifest, so obligationByName returns undefined for it.

claims.statement: The link that leaves a notification goes to that notification's overview once any answer is committed, and back to the dashboard while none is.
claims.quote:
export const leaveJourneyLink = (journey, answers) =>
  hasCommittedNotificationAnswers(answers)
    ? hubPath(journey.journeyId)
    : dashboardPath()

claims.statement: The question that asks which type of notification this is lives on the INS frontend, at /notification-type with the notification id and the current notification type ('live-animals') as query parameters.

Nothing in the set's flow sends a trader to the INS notification-type question: the entry guard's only target is the notification's own origin page, and the INS URL is handed to the journey flow for some other caller to use.
claims.quote:
export const journeyInsTypeQuestionUrl = (...args) =>
  configured().insTypeQuestionUrl(...args)
claims.note: The part's scope expects the entry guard to say when a trader is sent back to the INS type question. entry-guard.js returns only the origin page path, and the INS URL is exposed through journeyInsTypeQuestionUrl for a caller outside this part's files. Looked in entry-guard.js, journey-flow.js and routes-live-animals.js; the caller that uses it is not in this slice.

claims.note: CANCEL_AMEND_SLUG is 'cancel-amend' and the delete page's slug is 'delete', so the four paths are .../amend, .../cancel-amend, .../copy and .../delete.

claims.statement: Flow-only answers are kept in their own cookie, separate from the notification's answers, so none of them is part of the notification that is submitted.

flowOnlyAnswers: 'liveAnimalsFlowOnlyAnswers',
---

  Object.fromEntries(
    flowOnlyKeys()
      .filter(

      )
