claims.statement: The country of origin is always asked and always mandatory.
The country-of-origin subdivision code is always in scope and always optional.
Whether a region-of-origin code is required is itself always asked and mandatory.

The region-of-origin code is always in scope, and it switches from optional to mandatory when the trader answers yes to whether a region code is required; the reason given is that a region code is required.
claims.note: This is the only gate in the set that keeps an obligation in scope on both branches, so the answer is never purged when the requirement flips to no.

claims.statement: The arrival date at the port is always asked and always mandatory.
The port of entry is always asked and always mandatory.
The transporter type is always asked and always mandatory.
The commercial transporter record is asked, and mandatory, only when the transporter type is Commercial, and a stored commercial transporter is dropped when the type is switched away from Commercial.
The private transporter record is asked, and mandatory, only when the transporter type is Private, and goes out of scope otherwise.
The commercial and private transporter records are mutually exclusive: only one of the two can be in scope for any transporter type.
claims.quote: // Transporter type + mutually-exclusive address blocks

claims.statement: The means of transport is always asked and always mandatory.
The transport identification is always asked and always mandatory.
The transport document reference is always asked and always mandatory.

The countries transited are asked of rail and road consignments only, and even then they are never compulsory: a trader who passes through nowhere they can name leaves the list empty, the row reads Optional and submission is not held up.
claims.note: An existing ruling: the comment records it as a design release 1 decision.

claims.statement: A conditional obligation whose in-scope decision names no mandate is treated as mandatory, so an optional conditional answer must say 'optional' outright.
claims.quote:
// `status` must say 'optional' outright — `effectiveStatus` falls back to
// 'mandatory' for an implication that carries none.

claims.statement: The place of origin is always asked and always mandatory, and is stored as one composite address record.
The consignor is always asked and always mandatory.
The consignee is always asked and always mandatory.
The importer is always asked and always mandatory.
The place of destination is always asked and always mandatory.
The reason for import is always asked and always mandatory.
The purpose in the internal market is asked, and mandatory, only when the reason for import is internalMarket, and any stored purpose is dropped when the reason changes.
The destination country is asked, and mandatory, only when the reason for import is transit or transhipmentOrOnwardTravel, and is otherwise out of scope and purged.
claims.note: An existing ruling: the code records the V4 data dictionary (Confluence page 6497338582) as the authority for this rule.

claims.statement: The port of exit is asked, and mandatory, only when the reason for import is transit or temporaryAdmissionHorses, and is chosen from the same port list as the port of entry.
The exit date is asked, and mandatory, only when the reason for import is temporaryAdmissionHorses, and is otherwise out of scope and purged.
The internal reference number is always in scope and always optional.
The notification's approved reference number is assigned by the system when the notification is created and is never entered by a trader; it is mandatory but no page asks for it.
The notification's reference number is shaped GBN-AG-YY-XXXXXX, where the six-character body uses Crockford base32 (0-9 and A-Z without I, L, O or U).
A notification must hold at least one commodity line, and an empty list is refused under the code obligation.commodityLine.atLeastOne.
claims.note: The commodity lines group states no upper limit on the number of lines.

claims.statement: Every commodity line must carry a commodity code.
Every commodity line must carry a species Latin name.
A commodity line's species common name is optional.
Every commodity line must carry a number of animals.
A line's number of packages is asked only when that line's commodity code is in the package-count list, and even then it is optional.
The county parish holding number is asked, and mandatory, when any commodity line's code is in the CPH-required list, and is out of scope otherwise.
Whether the consignment contains unweaned animals is asked once for the whole notification, and only when any commodity line's code is in the unweaned list.

Each animal identifier record inside a commodity line must carry at least one of seven identifiers: a microchip, a passport, a tattoo, an ear tag, a horse name, identification details or a description; an empty record is refused under obligation.unitRecord.identifiersRequired.

The at-least-one-identifier floor is stood down unless more than one commodity line has a code in the identified list, so a consignment with a single identified line is not held to it at the collection level.
claims.quote:
floorAppliesToParent: moreThanOne(
      allowListed(commodityCode, identifiedCommodityCodes, null)
    )
---
 * The inner gate names the entries that would be asked; this wrapper stands
 * the whole rule down unless there are at least two of them, and otherwise
 * hands back the inner decision untouched with the same `fulfilmentIndexes`.
claims.note: mechanism: works on the commodity-lines collection. moreThanOne returns the inner allowListed decision only when it admits more than one entry, and otherwise reports out of scope.

claims.statement: A microchip is asked of an animal only on lines whose commodity code is in the microchip list, and is optional there.
A passport is asked of an animal only on lines whose commodity code is in the passport list, and is optional there.
A tattoo is asked of an animal only on lines whose commodity code is in the tattoo list, and is optional there.
An ear tag is asked of an animal only on lines whose commodity code is in the ear-tag list, and is optional there.
A horse name is asked of an animal only when its line's commodity code and species Latin name together are in the horse-name list, and is optional there.
claims.quote:
export const horseName = {
  id: HORSE_NAME_ID,
  name: 'horseName',
  within: unitRecord,
  status: 'optional',
  applyTo: allowListedPairs(
    commodityCode,
    speciesLatinName,
    horseNameCodeSpecies,
    unitRecord,
    [horseNameReason]
  )
}

claims.statement: Identification details are asked of an animal only on lines whose commodity code is outside the identified list, and are optional there.
A free-text description is asked of an animal only on lines whose commodity code is outside the identified list, and is optional there.
A permanent address is asked of an animal, and is mandatory, when its line's commodity code and species pair is in the permanent-address list.
claims.quote:
const permanentAddressPairGate = (reasons) =>
  allowListedPairs(
    commodityCode,
    speciesLatinName,
    permanentAddressCodeSpecies,
    unitRecord,
    reasons
  )

export const permanentAddress = {
  id: '3fcbd0e6-f708-4c2c-89ab-a56c7e8ea0b7',
  name: 'permanentAddress',
  within: unitRecord,
  status: 'mandatory',
  applyTo: permanentAddressPairGate([permanentAddressReason])
}

claims.statement: A trader can attach between zero and fifteen accompanying documents to a notification, and a sixteenth is refused under obligation.accompanyingDocument.tooMany.
The fifteen-document cap is enforced on the stored notification as well as on the page's Add affordance, so a saved notification holding more than the cap is still caught afterwards.
Each accompanying document must carry its own type, attachment type, reference and date of issue; all four are mandatory within a document.
A document's upload id and filename are optional, so a document can be recorded without a file attached.
The V4 data dictionary page still reads as if a notification can hold at most one accompanying document, and the obligation model is treated as the authority until that page is amended.
claims.note: An existing ruling recorded in code: a known disagreement with the V4 source, resolved in favour of the model.

claims.statement: Each document's instance id is a session-scoped counter value such as doc1 or doc2.
claims.quote: // Instance ids are session-scoped counter values (`doc1`, `doc2`, …).

claims.statement: A trader searching for a commodity gets one page of species grouped by CN code, with the total, the page number and the page size alongside.
claims.quote:
/**
 * One page of the species matching a term, grouped by CN code.
 *
 * @param {string} term - the search term.
 * @param {{page?: number, size: number}} paging - the zero-based page and its size.
 * @returns {Promise<{total: number, page: number, size: number, groups: Array<{code: string, species: Array<{latinName: string, commonName: string|null}>}>}>} the page of results.
 * @throws {import('@hapi/boom').Boom} 503 when reference data fails.
 */

claims.statement: The commodity search asks the reference data service for GET /commodities with the search term as q and the page and size as query parameters.
The species check asks the reference data service for POST /commodities/species-check with the commodity lines in the body.
The species check returns the commodity lines whose Latin name is not listed under their commodity code, and an empty list when every line's species is listed.
claims.quote:
/**
 * @param {Array<{code: string, latinName: string}>} lines - the lines to check.
 * @returns {Promise<Array<{code: string, latinName: string}>>} the lines whose
 *   Latin name is not listed under their code; empty when all are listed.
 * @throws {import('@hapi/boom').Boom} 503 when reference data fails.
 */

claims.statement: No species check is made at all when there are no commodity lines to check.
A species-check reply that carries no unlisted list is treated as a failure rather than as 'nothing unlisted'.

When the service is run in stub mode both the commodity search and the species check are answered from the service's own fixtures instead of reference data, and stub mode is never honoured in production.
A reference data failure is turned into a 503 'Reference data unavailable' naming the dataset that failed, either 'commodities' or 'species'.

Six commodity codes carry per-animal identifiers: cattle 0102 (ear tag, passport, tattoo), horses 0101 (microchip, passport and a horse name for Equus cabalus), swine 0103 (ear tag, tattoo), sheep 010410 (ear tag), goats 010420 (ear tag) and other live mammals 01061900 (microchip, passport, tattoo).
Those same six codes are the identified list, so a commodity line with any other code is treated as unidentified and asked for identification details and a description instead.
claims.quote: export const IDENTIFIED_CODES = Object.keys(COMMODITY_IDENTIFIERS)

claims.statement: The horse name is asked only for the species named Equus cabalus under commodity code 0101.

...
const HORSE_NAME_SPECIES = 'Equus cabalus'
...

Horses (0101) ask for a package count but do not require a CPH number; the three 0407 egg codes require a CPH number but ask for no package count.

claims.statement: Only three species need a permanent address, all under commodity code 01061900: Felis catus, Canis familiaris and Mustela putorius furo.
claims.note: Cats, dogs and ferrets, in Latin.

claims.statement: Four commodity codes carry a description: 0101 'Live horses, asses, mules and hinnies', 0102 'Live bovine animals', 01061900 'Other live animals' and 0301 'Live fish'.
Three commodity codes carry a short name: 0101 'Horse', 0102 'Cattle' and 0301 'Fish'.
Live fish, commodity code 0301, has a description and a short name but no identifiers, so a fish consignment is asked for identification details and a description rather than a tag or passport.

claims.note: 0301 is absent from COMMODITY_IDENTIFIERS, so it is outside IDENTIFIED_CODES and the notInUnionOf gates for identification details and description admit it.

claims.statement: The per-identifier code lists are derived from the one identifier table rather than written out, so a code that carries an identifier is always in that identifier's list.
claims.note: mechanism: turns the identifier table into per-identifier code lists, and into code-and-species pairs for an identifier that names a species.

claims.statement: A commodity search in stub mode matches a group when the term is a prefix of its CN code, and otherwise matches a species when every word of the term is a prefix of consecutive words of its Latin or common name.
claims.note: mechanism: the stub's own matching over the captured commodity fixtures; an empty term matches nothing by name, and a code prefix match returns the group's whole species list.

claims.statement: Stub search results are paged by slicing the flattened matches and then regrouping them by code, so a group can be split across two pages and the total counts species rather than groups.
claims.note: mechanism: paging over the stub's flattened code-and-species matches.

claims.statement: In stub mode a commodity line counts as unlisted when the captured fixtures hold no group with that code carrying that exact Latin name.
claims.quote:
const listedInStub = ({ code, latinName }) =>
  COMMODITY_GROUPS.some(
    (group) =>
      group.code === code &&
      group.species.some((species) => species.latinName === latinName)
  )

export const unlistedLinesInStub = (lines) =>
  lines.filter((line) => !listedInStub(line))

claims.statement: The stub's commodity groups are captured fixtures of the real reference data rather than a hand-written list.
claims.quote:
import { commodityGroups } from '../../../../services/_capture/fixtures.js'

export const COMMODITY_GROUPS = commodityGroups

claims.statement: The commodity service's own test support shows a ferret search returning two species under code 01061900, 'Mustela spp.' described as 'Weasels (including ermines, polecats, ferrets, and related species)' and 'Mustela putorius furo' described as 'Ferret'.
The commodity reference calls are tested at the network boundary, by mocking fetch rather than the service's own modules.
The system feature contributes one binding, the notification's approved reference number, held as a single value rather than a collection.
A commodity line is stored as a commodity code, a species Latin name, a species common name, a number of packages, a number of animals and a list of animal identifier records.
An accompanying document is stored as its type, its attachment type, its reference, a day-month-year date of issue and a filename.

A consignment party is stored as a name with a nested address, and some parties also carry a phone number and an email address; an address can be held either as free address lines with a country name or as lines with a town, postcode and country code.
claims.note: Two address shapes appear side by side in one finished notification, one keyed on `country` with free lines and one keyed on `countryCode` with a town and postcode.

claims.statement: When the destination country is in scope, the reason given is the code obligation.destinationCountry.applicable.becauseTransitOrTranshipment.
When the port of exit is in scope, the reason given is the code obligation.portOfExit.applicable.becauseTransitOrTemporaryAdmissionHorses.
When the exit date is in scope, the reason given is the code obligation.exitDate.applicable.becauseTemporaryAdmissionHorses.
When a passport is asked of an animal, the reason given is the code obligation.passport.applicable.becausePassportCommodity.
When a tattoo is asked of an animal, the reason given is the code obligation.tattoo.applicable.becauseTattooCommodity.
When an ear tag is asked of an animal, the reason given is the code obligation.earTag.applicable.becauseEarTagCommodity.
When a horse name is asked of an animal, the reason given is the code obligation.horseName.applicable.becauseHorseCommodity.
When identification details are asked of an animal, the reason given is the code obligation.identificationDetails.applicable.becauseUnidentifiedCommodity.
When a free-text description is asked of an animal, the reason given is the code obligation.description.applicable.becauseUnidentifiedCommodity.
When a permanent address is asked of an animal, the reason given is the code obligation.permanentAddress.applicable.becausePermanentAddressLine.
When where the permanent address came from is asked of an animal, the reason given is the code obligation.permanentAddressOrigin.applicable.becausePermanentAddressLine.
Every obligation carries a fixed UUID alongside its answer name, such as countryOfOrigin with id a01b2c3d-4e5f-4a6b-8c7d-9e0f1a2b3c4d.

claims.statement: The return carries four things in its query: fulfilment-id, handshake-token, addressId and landing.
The landing the address book names may be one of three: select, return or cancel.
A return naming a fulfilment id the service does not know is refused with a 400 Bad Request reading 'Unknown fulfilment', and the refusal is logged as 'Address return refused'.
A return naming a landing that is not select, return or cancel is refused with a 400 Bad Request reading 'Unknown landing'.
A return that names a landing other than cancel but no address is refused with a 400 Bad Request reading 'Missing address'.
A return that names no landing at all but does carry an address is treated as a selection.
A return that names neither a landing nor an address — someone simply coming back — takes the trader to that party's address picker, saves nothing and needs no handshake token.
claims.note: The token check comes after this branch, so a bare return is always honoured.

claims.statement: Every other return must carry the handshake token the service issued for that fulfilment id, and one that does not is refused with a 400 Bad Request reading 'Invalid handshake'.
claims.note: Security: this is the check that stops a return being replayed or forged for a party the trader never started a hand-off for. The token is compared against the trader's own cookie, so a return cannot be honoured in someone else's session.

claims.statement: A handshake token is used once: it is forgotten as soon as the return is accepted, and the whole cookie is dropped once no hand-off is outstanding.
A trader who cancels in the address book is returned to the notification overview, and nothing is saved.

An address returned as a selection is read back from the address book, copied onto the party as its answer, and the trader is taken to the Consignment addresses page with the added-address banner naming it.
An address returned with the 'return' landing is read back and the banner is shown, but it is not saved onto the party: the trader is taken to that party's address picker to choose it there.
claims.note: So 'select' means the address book chose the party's address for the trader, and 'return' means it only added the address to the book.

The CPH question is asked when any commodity line's code is on the CPH-required
list; a line with no code yet is ignored rather than counted as a match
(`anyAllowListed`).

claims.statement: The set records that the animal identifiers floor asks for a record per commodity line only on a consignment carrying more than one identified commodity line.
claims.quote:
The animal identifiers floor asks for a record per commodity
line only on a consignment carrying more than one identified commodity line
(`moreThanOne` over the identified-commodity allowlist).

claims.statement: The set records that the journey's feature bindings import the same obligation objects as the manifest, the shared object identity letting the fulfilment registry check that every leaf is owned once and that grouped binding paths match each within chain.
claims.quote:
The journey's feature bindings import the same obligation objects from this set.
This shared object identity lets the fulfilment registry check that every leaf is
owned once and that grouped binding paths match each `within` chain.

claims.statement: The set records that its allow-list test checks the commodity allow-lists against the set-owned reference service, each list's describe iterating its own allow-list and checking that a control value on no list leaves the obligation out of scope.
claims.quote:
checks the commodity allow-lists against the set-owned reference service; each
list's describe iterates its own allow-list and checks that a control value on
no list leaves the obligation out of scope

claims.statement: The set records that the package-count check instead iterates every code the captured catalogue serves and asserts the exact served codes the list leaves out, so a code new to the capture fails there, that one anti-drift describe pins every list's exact contents against an expected map, and that changing an allow-list on purpose means editing rules.js and updating the matching expected list in the same change.
claims.quote:
the package-count describe
instead iterates every code the set's captured catalogue serves and asserts
the exact served codes the list leaves out, which is where a code new to the
capture fails; one anti-drift describe pins every list's exact contents
against the expected map, so a single-file edit to a service list fails
there; to change an allow-list on purpose, edit it in
[`rules.js`](../services/commodities/rules.js) and update the matching expected list
in the test in the same change.

claims.statement: The set records that accompanying documents are capped at fifteen entries, the set manifest declaring the cardinality and the documents feature enforcing it on its write path.
claims.quote:
The document collection has a maximum of fifteen entries. The set manifest declares
the cardinality and the documents feature enforces it on its write path.
claims.note: Verified against the code: obligations/sections/documents.js:25 holds `maxEntries: 15` with error code `obligation.accompanyingDocument.tooMany`.

claims.statement: The set records that species come from MDM through reference-data and that the commodity rules — the identifier, package-count, permanent-address, unweaned, CPH-required and type rules — are set data that must match MDM's spelling exactly.
claims.quote:
Species come from MDM through reference-data. The rules in
[`rules.js`](../services/commodities/rules.js) are set data: the identifier,
package-count, permanent-address, unweaned, CPH-required and type rules. They must
match MDM's spelling exactly.

claims.statement: The set records that canonical fulfilment can hold values one backend projection cannot represent, that Mapper B layers its additional fields over Mapper A, and that a new obligation always needs a feature binding but only gets a mapper field when the target backend schema has a real home for it.
claims.quote:
Canonical fulfilment can contain values that one backend projection cannot
represent. Mapper B layers its additional fields over Mapper A. A new obligation
always needs a feature binding, but it only gets a mapper field when the target
backend schema has a real home for it.

claims.statement: The set records that Commodity details refuses a number of animals, and a number of packages, above 2,147,483,647 on each species line, because the animals backend holds those counts in Java Integer fields.
claims.ref: src/server/app/sets/live-animals/docs/limits.md:24 (A number of animals or packages above what the backend's field can hold is refused)
claims.quote:
Commodity details refuses a number of animals, and a number of packages,
above 2,147,483,647 on each species line. The animals backend's
`CommodityComplement.totalNoOfAnimals`, `CommodityComplement.totalNoOfPackages`
and `Species.noOfPackages` are Java `Integer` fields, so a count above their
range is rejected by the backend rather than stored.

claims.statement: The set records that the cap guards each line's own number and not the totals the backend derives from it, so several lines under one CN code can still sum past the field's range and nothing in the frontend refuses that.
claims.quote:
The cap guards each line's own number, not the totals the backend derives
from it.
claims.note: The ledger records this as a known, unrefused edge: "several lines under one CN code can still sum past the field's range, and nothing in the frontend refuses that".

claims.statement: The set records that grouped fulfilment tokens such as line0 and unit1 are positions in one canonical snapshot rather than durable record identifiers, so removing an earlier entry can renumber later entries.
claims.quote:
Grouped fulfilment tokens such as `line0` and `unit1` are positions in one canonical
snapshot, not durable record identifiers. Removing an earlier entry can renumber
later entries.

The dashboard's Welsh copy is a machine draft that a translator has not

The transporter list's Welsh added-transporter banner text is a machine
draft as well. A translator must review it in the same file, where it is a

The declaration's Welsh responsibility bullets both complete the "nes iddo naill

claims.statement: The set records that the permanent address page's Welsh copy and the consignment addresses page's permanent address section leaves are the same machine draft, neither to be shipped without Welsh Language Standards sign-off.
claims.quote:
The permanent address page's Welsh is a machine draft too. A translator must
review it in `journeys/linear/features/permanent-address/copy/copy.cy.js`.
The consignment addresses page's permanent address section leaves in
`journeys/linear/features/addresses/copy/copy.cy.js` are the same machine draft
and need the same review. Do not ship either without Welsh Language Standards

claims.statement: The set's copy-status record names no page-maturity level: it records which copy is unreviewed Welsh and nothing about whether a page's copy is agreed, the four maturity levels being recorded in features.md instead.

The repo's only record of agreed copy is the page-maturity level on each page.js (features.md:16, claim repo-frontend-p19-065) and page-design.md's one remark that a particular button and its copy are "agreed for now" (claim on the Commodity pages heading). Nothing in the repo records English copy as content-reviewed.

claims.statement: The live-animals journey records seven ordered flow sections, a flow section being an Overview group, and the sections together being the journey's one page order, the order Overview lists its tasks in.
claims.quote:
exports seven ordered `sections`. A flow
section is an Overview group, and the sections together are the journey's one page
order: the order Overview lists its tasks in.

claims.statement: The journey records that its required earlier answers, the ones Save and continue diverts to collect, are where the consignment is coming from and what is being imported.
claims.quote:
This journey's
required earlier answers are where the consignment is coming from and what is being
imported.

claims.statement: The journey records that the review section has the one authored section gate, requiring scope.readyForCheckYourAnswers, and that normal page gates are derived from meta.collects, scope and the required earlier answers.
claims.quote:
The `review` section has the one authored section
gate: it requires `scope.readyForCheckYourAnswers`. Normal page gates are derived
from `meta.collects`, scope and the required earlier answers.

claims.statement: The journey records that the consignment-parties section holds the CPH number page, then the permanent address page, then Consignment addresses, so each sub-page goes on to Consignment addresses and Consignment addresses goes on to the review page.
claims.quote:
The `consignment-parties` section holds the CPH number page, then the permanent address page,
then Consignment addresses, so each sub-page, marked `subPage: true` on its page identity, goes on
to Consignment addresses and Consignment addresses goes on to the review page.

claims.statement: The journey records that consignment-parties is a stable section id the journey spec and the prototype share, while its caption and group heading read "Addresses".
claims.quote: The section id `consignment-parties` is a stable id that the journey spec and the prototype share. Its caption and group heading read "Addresses".
claims.note: One of the few places the repo's ledger records the prototype itself as the reason for a name.

claims.statement: The journey records four flow-only keys kept in the session's flow-only store rather than canonical obligation fulfilment and never sent to the backend: declaration, commoditySearchRows, the values an add-transporter form is keeping after a refused save held per transporter type, and the name of the transporter a save has just added, read once by the transporter list for its success banner.
claims.quote:
`FLOW_ONLY_KEYS` contains `declaration` and `commoditySearchRows`, plus the two
keys the transport feature's own add-session module owns: the values an
add-transporter form is keeping after a refused save, held per transporter
type, and the name of the transporter a save has just added, read once by
the transporter list for its success banner. All four are kept in the
session's flow-only store rather than canonical obligation fulfilment, and
are never sent to the backend.

claims.statement: The journey records that the transport section lists one transporter step, the transporter list, and that the pages which add a transporter are detours off that list belonging to no section.
claims.quote:
The transport section lists one transporter step, the transporter list. The pages
that add a transporter are detours off that list and belong to no section.

claims.statement: The journey records twelve task rows, a task row grouping pages on Overview and being a submit-readiness unit rather than a flow section, deciding nothing about where Save and continue goes.
claims.quote:
exports twelve `taskRows`. A
task row groups pages on Overview and is a submit-readiness unit; it is not a flow
section, and it decides nothing about where Save and continue goes.

claims.statement: The journey records that most row status comes from the union of each page's collects, that parts narrows a row to a collection facet, and that the commodity line is split three ways — the selection on the commodities row, the numbers on the consignmentDetails row, the identifiers on the animalIdentification row — so each of the three pages over that one collection carries a status of its own.
claims.quote:
Most row status comes from the union of each page's `collects`. `parts` narrows a
row to a collection facet. The commodity line is split three ways — the selection
on the `commodities` row, the numbers on the `consignmentDetails` row, the
identifiers on the `animalIdentification` row — so each of the three pages over
that one collection carries a status of its own.

claims.statement: The journey records that the commodities row claims its facet with except rather than only, so a new member of the collection defaults to that row instead of falling out of all three, that conditional: true lets the hub hide a row that is not applicable, and that every row contributes to readyForCheckYourAnswers.
claims.quote:
The `commodities` row claims its
facet with `except` rather than `only`, so a new member of the collection defaults
to that row instead of falling out of all three. `conditional: true` lets the hub
hide a row that is not applicable. Every row contributes to
`readyForCheckYourAnswers`.

claims.statement: The journey records that applies is the escape hatch for a row whose parts cannot express its applicability, rowStatus reading Not applicable when it answers no whatever the parts would have rolled up to.
claims.quote:
`applies` is the escape hatch for a row whose parts cannot express its
applicability. `rowStatus` calls it with the answers and reads Not applicable when
it answers no, whatever the parts would have rolled up to.

claims.statement: The journey records that the animal identification row needs applies because its part, the commodityLines collection, is a structural group in scope from the moment the notification exists so the roll-up never reaches Not applicable, while the transit-countries row needs no applies because its answer leaves scope on its own.
claims.quote:
The animal
identification row needs it: its part is the `commodityLines` collection, a
structural group in scope from the moment the notification exists, so the roll-up
never reaches Not applicable and `conditional: true` on its own would leave the row
drawn. Reach for `applies` only when a scope condition genuinely cannot carry the
rule — the transit-countries row needs no `applies`, because its answer leaves
scope on its own.

claims.statement: The journey records that extraAnswerGiven is the second escape hatch, for a row owing an answer no part key can reach, because a leaf nested inside a collection such as the permanent address inside animalIdentifiers inside commodityLines has no part key of its own.
claims.quote:
`extraAnswerGiven` is the second escape hatch, for a row that owes an answer no
part key can reach. A scope key is a bare obligation name or a collection name, so
a leaf nested inside a collection — the permanent address inside `animalIdentifiers`
inside `commodityLines` — has no part key of its own.

claims.statement: The journey records that the addresses row declares extraAnswerGiven, a predicate over the answers and the evaluation, and that rowStatus holds that row at In progress rather than Completed while it answers false, whatever the parts roll up to.
claims.quote:
The addresses row declares
`extraAnswerGiven`, a predicate over the answers and the evaluation in the same
shape as `applies`, and `rowStatus` holds the row at In progress rather than
Completed while it answers false, whatever the parts roll up to.
claims.note: In progress is the internal row status; page-design.md records that the hub shows only Complete or To do on screen.

claims.statement: The journey records that the hub derives its groups from the flow sections, each section holding a task row's first page being a group headed by its caption and listing its task rows in the order of their first page, and that the session holds no record of how a notification was started.
claims.quote:
The hub derives its groups from the flow sections: each section that holds a task
row's first page is a group, headed by its caption, and lists its task rows in the
order of their first page. The sections are also the journey's page order, which
Save and continue follows from every start. The session holds no record of how a
notification was started.

claims.statement: The journey records the design-release decision that a trader may start any task on the notification in any order: no row on the hub is ever shut, every row is a link carrying a real status from the moment the notification exists, nothing on the page says "Cannot start yet", and a row that does not apply leaves the list instead.
claims.quote:
No row on the hub is ever shut: every row is a link carrying a real status from
the moment the notification exists, and nothing on the page says "Cannot start
yet". A row that does not apply to this consignment leaves the list instead
(`conditional`, and `applies` where the parts cannot express it).

claims.statement: The journey records that the review is not a task row at all: it is reached from a primary "Review and submit" button under the task list, beside the secondary "Return to dashboard", and is offered whatever the notification still owes, the review page rendering an unfinished notification and naming what is outstanding.
claims.quote:
The review is not a task row at all. Design release 1 reaches it from a primary
"Review and submit" button under the task list, beside the secondary "Return to
dashboard", and offers it whatever the notification still owes — the review page
renders an unfinished notification and names what is outstanding.

claims.statement: The journey records that the review section's authored gate on readyForCheckYourAnswers stands between the review page and submitting, the declaration refusing on the same verdict.
claims.quote:
The review
section's authored gate on `readyForCheckYourAnswers` still stands between that
page and submitting: the declaration refuses on the same verdict.

claims.statement: The journey records that the declaration is reachable only from the review: the review's Continue posts to /declaration with step=review, the review registers no POST of its own and GET /declaration redirects to the review, so the user has seen the review in its latest state before submitting.
claims.quote:
The declaration is reachable only from the review. The review's
Continue posts to `/declaration` with `step=review` - the review registers no
`POST` of its own, and `GET /declaration` redirects to the review. This is to
ensure that the user has seen the review in its latest state before submitting
the notification.

claims.statement: The journey records that the declaration page renders the concurrency token the review page rendered rather than the current one, and that the declaration submit works only while the current token still matches it, so a notification changed after the review rendered sends the trader back to the review with the "notification has been updated" banner.
claims.quote:
The declaration page renders the same concurrency
token as the review page (RT), rather than the current concurrency token. The
declaration submit (`step=declare`) only works if the current concurrency token
is still the same as RT, meaning that the notification is unchanged. If the
notification changed after the review rendered — another tab, another user — the
token no longer matches and the trader goes back to the review with the
"notification has been updated" banner (`?staleAction=1`).

claims.statement: The journey records that the review's GET records the concurrency token in the session and both declaration steps require the posted token to match it, so a token copied off another page cannot reach the declaration without the review.
claims.quote:
The review's GET also records the token in the session
(`check-answers/reviewed.js`), and both declaration steps require the posted
token to match it, so a token copied off another page cannot reach the
declaration without the review.
claims.note: Security-relevant: the ledger records this as the control that stops a declaration being reached without the review.

claims.statement: The journey records that a refused Continue or Submit goes back with ?refused=1, which moves focus to the review's error summary, and that the review names every refusal itself, still-scanning documents included.
claims.quote:
A refused Continue or Submit goes back with
`?refused=1`, which moves focus to the review's error summary; the review names
every refusal itself, still-scanning documents included.

claims.statement: The journey records that letting every row be startable puts the cost on the pages rather than the hub: a page behind a row has to render and save sensibly when nothing else has been answered, and where there is genuinely nothing to ask yet the page says so itself.
claims.quote:
That puts the cost on the pages, not the hub: a page behind a row has to render
and save sensibly when nothing else has been answered. Where there is genuinely
nothing to ask yet the page says so itself

claims.statement: The journey records that the consignment details page redirects to the commodity question when the notification holds no line, and that the transit countries page sends a load or any submit to the overview, saving nothing, when the means of transport leaves transit countries out of scope.
claims.quote:
the consignment-details page
([`consignment-details.controller.js`](../journeys/linear/features/commodities/consignment-details/consignment-details.controller.js))
redirects to the commodity question when the notification holds no line, and
the transit countries page
([`transit-countries.controller.js`](../journeys/linear/features/transport/transit-countries/transit-countries.controller.js))
sends a load or any submit to the overview, saving nothing, when the means of
transport leaves transit countries out of scope.

claims.statement: The journey records that its entry guard owns the redirect policy before handlers run, along with the Import Notification Service's type question URL the gateway passes to configureJourneyFlow().
claims.quote:
owns the journey's redirect
policy before handlers run and the Import Notification Service's type question
(`insTypeQuestionUrl`), which the gateway passes to `configureJourneyFlow()`.

claims.statement: The journey records a table of where Back opens for each way the trader arrived: Save and continue on another page opens that page carrying the places beneath it; an Overview task row or review button opens Overview; a review Change link or error link opens the review; a dashboard card (View or Amend) opens the dashboard; starting a new notification opens the dashboard from the first page; arriving from the Import Notification Service opens its type question for this notification from the first page; and nothing the journey knows opens Overview.
claims.quote:
| Save and continue on another page     | That page, carrying the places beneath it            |
| An Overview task row or review button | Overview                                             |
| A review Change link or error link    | The review                                           |
| A dashboard card (View or Amend)      | The dashboard                                        |
| Start a new notification              | The dashboard, from the first page                   |
| The Import Notification Service       | Its type question for this notification, first page  |
| Nothing the journey knows             | Overview (the first page: see the entry guard below) |

claims.statement: The journey records that following a Back link ends nothing: a later Save and continue goes on to the next page that applies, adding the page saved to the trail, so Back steps through the visited pages in reverse, while Save and return to overview still goes to the overview.
claims.quote:
Following a Back link does not end anything: a later Save and continue goes on to the
next page that applies, adding the page saved to the trail, so Back steps through the
visited pages in reverse. Save and return to overview still goes to the overview.

claims.statement: The journey records that a round trip to a sub-page keeps where the trader came from, so the page that opened it still goes Back where it did before, the permanent address page, add transporter and a picker's View link each carrying the trail out and back.
claims.quote:
A round trip to a sub-page keeps where the trader came from, so the page that opened
it still goes Back where it did before: the permanent address page, add transporter
and a picker's View link each carry the trail out and back.

claims.statement: The journey records that the identification page's no-commodity-line guard carries the trail on to What are you importing? so Back there opens the page the trader came from, and that What are you importing? opened by Commodity details or Identification details saves back to the page that opened it carrying the trail, its Back opening that page.
claims.quote:
The identification page's no-commodity-line guard carries the trail on to What
are you importing?, so Back there opens the page the trader came from. What are you
importing? opened by Commodity details or Identification details saves back to the page
that opened it, carrying the trail, and its Back opens that page.

claims.statement: The journey records that a return value naming a page not allowed to open a sub-page is refused, logged and ignored.
claims.quote:
A return value that is
not one of the pages allowed to open this sub-page is refused, logged and ignored.

claims.statement: The journey records that the county parish holding number page is the exception to the trail rules: its Back always answers the consignment addresses page carrying the trail however the page was reached, and its Save and continue answers the same page unless a required earlier answer is still missing, in which case it answers the page asking for that answer.
claims.quote:
The county parish holding number page is the exception: its Back always answers the
consignment addresses page, carrying the trail, however the page was reached, and its
Save and continue answers the consignment addresses page as the next step that applies
— the same page, carrying the trail — unless a required earlier answer is still
missing, in which case it answers the page that asks for that answer instead.

claims.statement: The journey records that the Back fallback is the overview except on the first page, where it is the dashboard until an answer is entered and then the overview, and on the review, where it is the overview on a draft or an amendment and the dashboard on a submitted notification, including the one shown after an amendment is cancelled.
claims.quote:
The fallback is the overview, except on the first
page (the dashboard until an answer is entered, then the overview: `leaveJourneyLink` in
`entry-guard.js`) and on the review (the overview on a draft or an amendment, the
dashboard on a submitted notification, including the one shown after an amendment is
cancelled).

claims.statement: The journey records that returning from the Import Notification Service's address book lands on a fixed address carrying no trail, and that the Consignment addresses page is the only page whose Back goes to the Overview whatever the trail after that return, its Save and continue still going on from it.
claims.quote:
Returning from the Import Notification Service's address book lands on a fixed address
that carries no trail. The Consignment addresses page (the Overview task "Consignment addresses")
is the only page whose Back goes to the Overview whatever the
trail, after that return; Save and continue still goes on from it.

claims.statement: The journey records that the hub is somewhere the user chooses to go — through the Save and return to overview button, from Overview's own address, from an Overview task, or by opening the notification from the dashboard — while Save and continue goes to the next page that applies in the journey's one page order from every start and past the last page that applies goes to the review page.
claims.quote:
The hub is somewhere the user chooses to go: through the secondary "Save and
return to overview" button on the pages that offer it
([How a page ends](page-design.md#how-a-page-ends)), from Overview's address, from an
Overview task, or by opening the notification from the dashboard.

claims.statement: The journey records that a notification is created by the dashboard's create POST or by the start entry at <set>/start, which the Import Notification Service's type question opens, through one helper that redirects to the origin page with the dashboard or the Import Notification Service as the first place on the trail.
claims.quote:
A notification is created by the dashboard's create POST or by the start entry
(`<set>/start`, which the Import Notification Service's type question opens), through one
helper in
[`features/dashboard/controller.js`](../journeys/linear/features/dashboard/controller.js)
that redirects to the origin page with the dashboard or the Import Notification Service
as the first place on the trail.

claims.statement: The journey records that the start entry sits outside /notifications/ so the entry guard never sees it, and that the origin page is the journey entry.
claims.quote:
The start entry sits outside `/notifications/`, so the
entry guard never sees it. The origin page is the journey entry.

claims.statement: The journey records that the entry guard admits a request only when the journey carries an answer the user entered, system-populated obligations and flow-only keys such as declaration never counting as user answers, and that a journey with none is sent to the origin page, as is a request for Overview, the review, the declaration or the confirmation page, each redirect being logged once with the journey id and the requested path.
claims.quote:
The guard admits a request when the journey carries an answer the user entered.
System-populated obligations and flow-only keys such as `declaration` never count
as user answers. A journey with none (a deep link to an id this session never
created, or a draft with nothing saved) is sent to the origin page, and a request
for Overview, the review, the declaration or the confirmation page is sent there
too. Each redirect is logged once with the journey id and the requested path.

claims.statement: The journey records that a notification which cannot be found at all is answered by the guard itself with the service's standard page not found on every page, the review included, before any page runs, and is never sent to the origin page or the notification list.
claims.quote:
A
notification that cannot be found at all is answered by the guard itself with the
service's standard page not found (404), on every page, the review included,
before any page runs, and is sent nothing to the origin page or the notification
list.

claims.statement: The journey records that the origin page and its children and the amend, cancel-amend, copy and delete actions are exempt from the entry guard so there is no redirect loop, and that an exempt path's own page answers not found the same way.
claims.quote:
The origin page and its children, and the amend, cancel-amend, copy and
delete actions, are exempt from the guard, so there is no redirect loop. An
exempt path's own page answers not found the same way.

claims.statement: The journey records that a journey the guard bounces to the origin page carries no trail, so the origin page's Back is the dashboard until an answer is entered, and that the guard sends the request on to What are you importing? like any other start.
claims.quote:
A journey the guard bounces to the origin page carries no trail, so the origin page's

the dashboard.

the declaration, including a refusal that comes back through it; from the confirmation

claims.statement: The journey records that a caption must be passed the size matching its heading and nothing may sit between the two, because the caption's own bottom margin collapses from the tablet breakpoint so it reads as a caption only when it is the element directly above the heading.

nothing sit between the two: the caption carries its own bottom margin, which
collapses from the tablet breakpoint, so it only reads as a caption when it is the
element directly above the heading.

claims.statement: The repo records the decision that pre-commit is cheap, running lint-staged to format and auto-fix lint problems on the staged files only with no build and no tests, so the fixes land in the commit that caused them, because by push time the code is already committed and a fixer would be writing changes the commit does not contain.
claims.quote:
**`pre-commit` is cheap.** It runs `lint-staged`, which formats and
auto-fixes lint problems on the staged files only. No build, no tests. The
fixes land in the commit that caused them, which is the whole point of doing
it here: by push time the code is already committed, so a fixer would be
writing changes the commit does not contain.

claims.statement: The repo records that pre-push is the full gate, running the format check, lint and the unit suite, which builds the frontend first.

check, lint and the unit suite (which builds the frontend first, via
`pretest`).

claims.statement: The repo records why the slow half of the gate sits on pre-push rather than pre-commit: the suite is about 3,400 tests with coverage on top of a production webpack build, mostly fixed startup cost that does not shrink for a small change, and charging that to every commit is what teaches people to reach for --no-verify, which skips the cheap format and lint checks as well, while a push is the first point the work affects anyone else.
claims.quote:
The slow half is on pre-push rather than pre-commit on purpose. The suite is
~3,400 tests with coverage on top of a production webpack build, mostly
fixed startup cost that does not shrink for a small change. Charging that to
every commit — including the ones you are about to squash — is what teaches
people to reach for `--no-verify`, which skips the cheap format and lint
checks as well. A push is the first point the work affects anyone else, so
the gate sits there.

claims.statement: The repo records that when the pre-push hook reports there is nothing to re-run, the workspace's SonarCloud pre-push gate has already run format, lint and the suite for that exact commit and left a marker naming the verified SHA under .cache/, so the hook skips rather than repeating it, and that without that workspace the full gate always runs locally.
claims.quote:
If the hook reports that there is "nothing to re-run", the SonarCloud
pre-push gate in the
[trade-imports-workspace](https://github.com/DEFRA/trade-imports-workspace)
tooling has already run format, lint and the suite for that exact commit and
left a marker naming the verified SHA under `.cache/`; the hook skips rather
than repeating all of it.

claims.statement: After a valid add in the address-book mode, the add in progress is cleared, the success banner '<name> address added to your address book' is set, and the user lands on page 1 of the address book list on the tab of the chosen address type.

claims.note: The success is logged with the organisation id, address id and address type.

claims.statement: After a valid add in the role-handshake mode, the browser is sent to the journey's return URL carrying the new address id and the landing the user chose: select for 'Save and select', return for 'Save and return to address page'.
claims.quote:
payload.action === ADDRESS_LANDING.RETURN
    ? ADDRESS_LANDING.RETURN
    : ADDRESS_LANDING.SELECT
claims.note: The hand-back is logged with the organisation id, journey type, notification id, fulfilment id, address id and landing.

claims.statement: When the address-book service refuses the new address as invalid, the add page shows the service's errors against the form fields with status 400, keeping the entered values, and the refusal is logged at warn.

claims.statement: When saving the new address fails for any other reason, the add page is shown again with a recoverable-error message and status 500, keeping the entered values, and the failure is logged at error.
claims.quote: logger.error({ err, ...logContext }, 'Failed to create address')
claims.note: An HTTP error already raised as a Boom error (such as reference data unavailable) is passed on instead of re-rendering.

claims.statement: In the address-book mode the values entered and the roles ticked are kept for the add in progress on every post, so after a refused save the user can go Back to the address-type page, choose the same type again and see the address, contact details and ticked role they entered.

claims.statement: The role-handshake mode keeps nothing in the add in progress: the form opens empty each time the journey opens it.

claims.statement: A saved address shows in the address book list with each stored postal line on its own line, every line but the last ending in a comma, and its country in a separate column.

`)

claims.statement: A saved address's country is shown by its name from the country list, and by its code when the code is not in the list.

claims.statement: A search term matches a country when the country's name contains the term, ignoring case and surrounding spaces; a blank term matches no country.

countries

The notification published to other services is a GBN-AG document with two halves: an exchanged document and a specified consignment.

The published specified consignment carries the consignor, consignee, despatch, delivery, importer and carrier parties, the origin country, the unloading base port, the final destination, the main carriage transport movements, the transit countries, whether the consignment holds unweaned animals, and the consignment items.

A published trade line item carries a description, the scientific and common species names, a product unit quantity per delivery, an item quantity per package, and the individual animals, each with a name and a list of identifiers.
Each animal identifier is published as a type code and a content value, so the kind of identifier (ear tag, passport and so on) travels as a code beside the number.
claims.note: No test in this slice reads the identifier type codes, so which codes are sent is not proven here.

claims.statement: A published party carries an identifier, a URL id, a name, a party role code and a list of party type codes, each coded value being a value with an optional URL id and name.

A published country carries a code, its subordinate country sub-divisions and a region of origin code; a published location carries an identifier, a URL id, a name and a type code; and a published transport movement carries a numeric mode code and the transport contract documents.

The canned submission event the suite keeps carries a flat summary of the notification — reference number, status, point of entry and a commodities list of species name and number of animals — not the GBN-AG document the outbox event model describes.
claims.note: An ambiguity recorded, not settled: outbox-event-document.ts:9 types `data` as GbnAgEventData, the model names the event type uk.gov.defra.imports.notification.NotificationSubmitted (outbox-event-document.ts:155) where the canned file says NotificationSubmitted, and the canned file also carries an eventId and a publishedAt that the model does not. No spec in this slice reads the canned file. The reconciler should decide which shape is current.

claims.statement: The security scan is dynamic application security testing with OWASP ZAP as a proxy: Playwright drives real signed-in journeys through it instead of letting ZAP crawl, so ZAP attacks what a real session touched.
claims.quote: A DAST (Dynamic Application Security Testing) scan using [OWASP ZAP](https://www.zaproxy.org/) as a proxy. Playwright drives real authenticated journeys through it rather than letting ZAP crawl, so it observes what a real session touches and then attacks that.

claims.statement: Scan coverage is traffic-driven, so any route no spec drives is invisible to the scan; the attacking corpus is therefore curated by hand rather than generated.
claims.quote: Coverage is therefore **traffic-driven**: a route no spec drives is invisible to the scan. That is why the `@active` corpus is curated by hand rather than generated.
claims.note: Stated in general terms: the weakness is one of coverage, not of any particular route.

claims.statement: There are two security profiles: a passive one that runs the end-to-end suite without the attacking specs and does not attack, and an attacking one that runs only the attacking specs and is deliberate and docker-compose only.
claims.quote:
| `security`        | The e2e suite, excluding `@active` | No — passive only | Cheap, run broadly              |
| `security:active` | The `@active` suite only           | Yes               | Deliberate; docker-compose only |

claims.statement: The attacking specs are kept out of the passive profile because they walk the same journeys a second time and include destructive steps.
claims.ref: docs/security.md, note under the Profiles table
claims.quote: `@active` is excluded from the passive profile because it walks the same journeys a second time and includes destructive steps.

claims.statement: The attacking profile is refused on the CDP platform: the attacking specs delete notifications, documents and dead-letter messages and the scan refires each with fuzzed payloads, which is acceptable against a throwaway stack and destructive against a shared one, so the entrypoint fails the run instead.
claims.quote: The `@active` suite deletes notifications, documents and DLQ messages, and the active scan re-fires each with fuzzed payloads — fine against a disposable stack, destructive against a shared one. `entrypoint.sh` writes to `FAILED` rather than running it.

claims.statement: Guarding only the production environment is not enough to keep the attacking profile off shared environments, because such a guard would still have let dev, test and perf-test run it.
claims.quote: The `throwIfProdEnvironment` guard is no help here: it stops `prod` alone, so `dev`, `test` and `perf-test` would all have run.

claims.statement: The scan runs in three lanes that do not share a configuration or a target: locally against the localhost stack in either profile, from a GitHub Action against a stack on the runner in the attacking profile, and on the CDP portal against a deployed environment in the passive profile only.
claims.quote: | **CDP portal**    | `PROFILE` env var → `entrypoint.sh`                                                                         | `playwright.config.ts`                | deployed `${ENVIRONMENT}` | `security` or `<domain>:security` only  |

claims.statement: The GitHub Action that runs the attacking scan runs at 01:00 UTC on weekdays, and can also be started by hand.
claims.ref: docs/security.md, paragraph after the lanes table (line 28)
claims.quote: The GitHub Action runs at 01:00 UTC on weekdays, and on manual dispatch.
claims.note: Replaces the earlier claim that the Action was manual dispatch only with its nightly schedule switched off.

claims.statement: The attacking scan's report is published to a public GitHub Pages site under a dated path and is password-protected for that reason, and reports older than seven days are deleted.
claims.quote: Its report publishes to GitHub Pages under `security-active/<date>/`, password-protected via the `ZAP_REPORT_PASSWORD` secret because that Pages site is otherwise public. Reports older than 7 days are pruned.
claims.note: The password itself is a repository secret and is not in the source; nothing here names a value.

claims.statement: Security testing is a dynamic scan with OWASP ZAP as a proxy, with Playwright driving real authenticated journeys through it rather than letting ZAP crawl.
claims.quote: A DAST (Dynamic Application Security Testing) scan using [OWASP ZAP](https://www.zaproxy.org/) as a proxy. Playwright drives real authenticated journeys through it rather than letting ZAP crawl, so it observes what a real session touches and then attacks that.

claims.statement: Security coverage is traffic-driven: a route no spec drives is invisible to the scan, which is why the attacking corpus is curated by hand.
claims.quote: Coverage is therefore **traffic-driven**: a route no spec drives is invisible to the scan. That is why the `@active` corpus is curated by hand rather than generated.

claims.statement: There are two security profiles: a passive one that runs the whole end-to-end suite without attacking, and an attacking one that runs only the curated corpus and is for deliberate use against the local stack.
claims.quote:
| `security`        | The e2e suite, excluding `@active` | No — passive only | Cheap, run broadly              |
| `security:active` | The `@active` suite only           | Yes               | Deliberate; docker-compose only |

claims.statement: The attacking profile is refused on the deployed CDP environments, because the curated corpus deletes records and the attack re-fires each deletion with fuzzed payloads.

claims.statement: CDP blocks direct calls to its back-end services from outside its network, so a laptop run sets CDP_LOCAL=true, which sends those calls through the protected ephemeral gateway and needs a developer API key sent as x-api-key; the run stops at once if the key is missing, and a CDP Portal run needs neither setting.
claims.quote:
CDP blocks direct calls to its backend services from outside its network, so
global set-up cannot reach the backend or the address book without
`CDP_LOCAL=true`. That setting sends those calls through the protected
ephemeral gateway, which needs `DEVELOPER_API_KEY` as `x-api-key`. The run
stops at once if `CDP_LOCAL=true` and the key is missing. The CDP Portal run
sits inside CDP and needs neither.

Test types are selected by tag, not by directory: `npm test` runs a domain's

claims.statement: @duplicated-in-frontend marks an end-to-end spec whose behaviour the frontend's own FIT suite also proves, so a reader knows the check exists in both places.
claims.quote: `@duplicated-in-frontend` marks an end-to-end spec whose behaviour the frontend's own FIT suite also proves, so a reader knows the check exists in both places.

claims.statement: The suite does not wipe the database before it runs and does not need to, because every spec creates the state it asserts on through the back-end API, scoped to that run, so the specs pass against a database holding earlier runs' records.
claims.quote:
The suite does not wipe the database before it runs, and does not need to.
Every spec creates the state it asserts on through the front door (the
backend API), scoped to that run, so the specs pass against a database that
already holds the records of earlier runs.

claims.statement: A spec asserts which journey page is open through the page object's expected URL pattern, which matches the page whichever trail its address carries, and asserts an exact trail through the on-trail pattern or exact URL built from the page objects' own slugs; a spec never types a from query itself.
claims.quote:
- Which page is open: the page object's `expectedUrlPattern(reference)`. It matches the page whichever trail its address carries.
- The exact trail: the page object's `expectedUrlPatternOnTrail(reference, places)` for a `toHaveURL` matcher, or `expectedUrlOnTrail(reference, places)` for an exact `href` value. Pass the page objects' own `slug`s and the `TRAIL_START` places. A spec never types a `?from=` query.

claims.statement: An assertion two specs share lives in a shared checks module, and a flow or page object holds no assertion.
claims.quote: - An assertion two specs share lives in a `*-checks.ts` module under `page-objects/shared/` (`journey-checks.ts`, `type-ahead-checks.ts`). A flow or page object holds no assertion.

claims.statement: Visual regression tests guard rendered composition — layout, spacing, colour and typography as the user sees the page — by comparing screenshots against committed baseline images and failing if any pixels differ outside the masked regions.
claims.quote: Visual regression tests (tagged `@visual`) guard rendered composition — layout, spacing, colour, and typography as the user sees the page. They compare screenshots against committed baseline images and fail if any pixels differ outside the masked regions.

claims.statement: Baselines are committed beside their spec files, and each platform needs its own baseline, both of which are updated when a visual change is intentional.
claims.quote: Baselines are stored alongside their spec files in `*-snapshots/` directories and must be committed. Each platform requires its own baseline — update both when visual changes are intentional.

claims.statement: Visual specs run headless whatever the project setting, because headed mode uses the operating system's font rendering, which produces pixel differences against a headless baseline.
claims.quote: Visual specs run headless whatever the project setting, because headed mode uses OS font rendering, which produces pixel differences against a headless baseline.

claims.statement: On macOS a visual run launches the browser itself with legacy scroll bars, because Chromium sizes a native select's arrow box from the macOS scroll bar style and overlay scroll bars draw every native select four pixels narrower, which failed a baseline made on a trackpad once a mouse was plugged in.
claims.quote: Visual specs import `test` from `@fixtures/visual`. On macOS it launches Playwright's headless shell with legacy scroll bars (`-AppleShowScrollBars Always`) and connects to it over CDP. Chromium sizes a native `<select>` arrow box from the macOS scroll bar style, and with the default "Show scroll bars: Automatically" setting that style follows whether a mouse is connected: overlay scroll bars on a trackpad alone, legacy ones with a mouse. Overlay scroll bars draw every native select 4px narrower, so a `*-darwin.png` baseline made on a laptop's trackpad failed with a mouse plugged in (704 pixels on the no-JavaScript import reason page), and the other way round. Playwright's own launch refuses an argument that does not start with `-`, so the fixture starts the browser itself. On Linux the fixture is the shared one, unchanged.
claims.note: mechanism: the visual fixture's own browser launch, for the macOS baseline. Names the no-JavaScript import reason page as the page whose baseline differed.

claims.statement: The declaration visual specs set the date of declaration to a fixed string before the screenshot rather than masking it, because the server writes today's date into the page text and a mask is as wide as that text; the date's strong emphasis is proved by the declaration end-to-end specs instead.
claims.quote: The declaration specs set the date of declaration to a fixed string before the screenshot instead of masking it, because the server writes today's date into the page text and a mask is as wide as that text, which changes with the day and month. `freezeDatePickersAt` does not reach that text: it stops the browser clock and moves each date picker's served bounds, and changes nothing the server has already written. The date's strong emphasis is proved by the declaration e2e specs.

claims.statement: Only the animals and plants domains have visual specs.
claims.quote: `animals` and `plants` have `@visual` specs.

claims.statement: Baselines are regenerated by two commands, one for the host-rendered darwin image and one for the container-rendered linux image CI uses, each running every visual spec and writing the updated snapshot into the working tree for commit.
claims.quote:
Regenerate the E2E baseline against the stack frontend with
`npm run test:visual:update:macos` for the host-rendered `*-darwin.png` image and
`npm run test:visual:update:linux` for the container-rendered `*-linux.png` image
used by CI. Both commands run every `@visual` spec and write the
updated snapshot into the working tree for commit.

claims.statement: The Linux baseline script points the service URLs at host.docker.internal and maps localhost to the host, because inside the container localhost is the container.
claims.quote: The Linux script points the service URLs at `host.docker.internal`, because inside the container `localhost` is the container. It also runs the container with `--add-host=localhost:host-gateway`, which maps `localhost` to the host, so any URL the script does not override and that still names `localhost` reaches the stack too.

claims.statement: Every full-page screenshot of a notification page masks the whole status strip, not the reference alone, so the masked box stays a fixed size while the notification reference is minted per run; the strip's own content is covered by an end-to-end spec.
claims.quote:
Every full-page screenshot of a notification page masks the whole status strip. It renders
from the first request and holds the notification reference, which is minted per run. The
whole strip is masked, not the reference alone, so the masked box stays a fixed size. The
strip's own content is covered by `tests/animals/e2e/features/reference-strip.spec.ts`.

claims.statement: A calendar screenshot depends on today's date twice — the browser's today picks the month and highlighted day, and the server's today sets each picker's minimum and maximum date — so the suite stops the browser clock on a fixed day and moves the served bounds by the same number of days.
claims.quote:
A calendar screenshot depends on today's date twice: the browser's today picks the month and
the highlighted day, and the server's today sets each picker's `data-min-date` and
`data-max-date`. `freezeDatePickersAt` (`utils/frozen-date-picker.ts`) stops the browser clock
on a fixed day and moves the served bounds by the same number of days, so the calendar looks
as it would if that day were today.

claims.statement: The security scan is a dynamic application security test using OWASP ZAP as a proxy, with Playwright driving real authenticated journeys through it rather than letting ZAP crawl, so it observes what a real session touches and then attacks that.
claims.quote: A DAST (Dynamic Application Security Testing) scan using [OWASP ZAP](https://www.zaproxy.org/) as a proxy. Playwright drives real authenticated journeys through it rather than letting ZAP crawl, so it observes what a real session touches and then attacks that.

claims.statement: Security coverage is traffic-driven, so a route no spec drives is invisible to the scan, which is why the active corpus is curated by hand rather than generated.
claims.quote: Coverage is therefore **traffic-driven**: a route no spec drives is invisible to the scan. That is why the `@active` corpus is curated by hand rather than generated.

claims.statement: There are two security profiles: a passive scan across the end-to-end suite excluding the active corpus, cheap enough to run broadly, and a passive plus scoped active scan against the active suite alone, which attacks and runs on docker-compose only.
claims.quote:
| `security`        | The e2e suite, excluding `@active` | No — passive only | Cheap, run broadly              |
| `security:active` | The `@active` suite only           | Yes               | Deliberate; docker-compose only |

claims.statement: The active suite is excluded from the passive profile because it walks the same journeys a second time and includes destructive steps.
claims.quote: `@active` is excluded from the passive profile because it walks the same journeys a second time and includes destructive steps.

claims.statement: The scan runs in three lanes: locally against the localhost stack on both profiles and per domain except plants, as a GitHub Action against a stack on the runner for the full active corpus, and from the CDP Portal against the deployed environment for the passive profile only.
claims.quote: | **Local**         | `npm run test:docker-compose[:<domain>]:security`, `npm run test:docker-compose[:<domain>]:security:active` | `playwright.docker-compose.config.ts` | localhost stack           | both; each also per domain (not plants) |

claims.statement: The active profile is refused on CDP because the active suite deletes notifications, documents and dead-letter messages and the scan re-fires each with fuzzed payloads, which is fine against a disposable stack and destructive against a shared one; the production guard is no help because it stops prod alone, so dev, test and perf-test would all have run.
claims.quote: **`security:active` is refused on CDP.** The `@active` suite deletes notifications, documents and DLQ messages, and the active scan re-fires each with fuzzed payloads — fine against a disposable stack, destructive against a shared one. `entrypoint.sh` writes to `FAILED` rather than running it. The `throwIfProdEnvironment` guard is no help here: it stops `prod` alone, so `dev`, `test` and `perf-test` would all have run.

claims.statement: The scheduled security scan workflow runs at 01:00 UTC on weekdays as well as on manual dispatch, and calls the workspace's active-scan workflow.

on:

claims.note: Ambiguity recorded, not resolved: docs/security.md:28 and README.md:524 both say the scan is manual dispatch only and the schedule stays disabled, while the workflow file carries an enabled weekday cron.

claims.quote: 2. Bring up ZAP too — additive, and waits for healthchecks so it returns only once ZAP is accepting requests: `tim docker up --profile security`

claims.quote: Full `security:active` is the authoritative clean bill of health. Per-domain active sets `ZAP_SCOPE` so the no-traffic gate only covers that domain's contexts; the report is labelled as scoped.

claims.statement: Each run clears the ZAP report directory first, so running two domains back to back keeps only the second domain's report.
claims.quote: Each run clears `zap-report/` first, so running two domains back to back keeps only the second domain's report.

claims.quote: > **Docker Desktop for Mac:** ZAP needs `network_mode: host` to resolve the stack's `localhost` OIDC redirects. OrbStack supports this out of the box; Docker Desktop needs 4.34+ with host networking enabled in Settings (off by default).

claims.quote: ZAP runs as part of the shared workspace stack (`docker/stack/security.compose.yml`). On CDP the same plan files and gate are reused, with ZAP as an in-process daemon rather than a container.

claims.statement: The Defra ID stub is observed passively and never attacked because it is a temporary sign-in stub the team does not own, while the service's own sign-in and sign-in-oidc handlers are in scope since the OIDC callback and its redirect parameter outlive the stub.
claims.quote: | `trade-imports-defra-id-stub` (3007) | A temporary sign-in stub we do not own. Observed passively, never attacked. Our own `/auth/sign-in` and `/auth/sign-in-oidc` handlers **are** in scope — the OIDC callback and its `redirect` parameter outlive the stub. |

claims.statement: The CDP uploader is not scanned because the browser posts uploads to the frontend, which forwards them server-side, so the uploader never enters the site tree.
claims.quote: | `cdp-uploader` (7337)                | A platform component. The browser posts uploads to the frontend, which forwards them server-side, so the uploader never enters the site tree.                                                                             |
